#4277. 10 Reasons You Will Be Playing GTA 6 For More Than a Decade

Ronald is a video game journalist with more than 10 years of experience in the industry, working on several of the most important Spanish websites.

After a week of GTA 6's availability, there are two things I can say with complete certainty: first, Red Dead Redemption 2 is the best thing that could have happened to Rockstar, and second, we'll be following Jason, Lucia, and company for a long time.

The developer's magnum opus offers an immersive and expansive world that will take us many years to fully decipher, so I can already imagine how numerous ecosystems, from video games to content creation, will be completely permeated until, perhaps, the release of the seventh installment.

However, far from wanting to theorize about future adventures of the IP, the priority is to appreciate the one we already have in our hands and savor it slowly, since that's what the game itself aims for by offering a story, mechanics, and context that evolve at a much more leisurely pace.

Therefore, in order to play fortune teller and anticipate how long we will be hanging around Leonida, I invite you to read this list of ten reasons you will be playing GTA 6 for more than a decade.

Analyzing the evolution of video games, especially considering their affinity with technology, is an activity that involves intertemporal comparisons, and GTA 6 has established itself as the generational benchmark we look to when we want to see if the industry has moved forward.

Titles like The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, BioShock, The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim, and The Last of Us Part II have stood for years as monoliths of their respective genres and platforms, garnering enduring attention that regularly draws us back to reaffirm their influence.

Thus, considering the technical, graphical, and design marvel that is Rockstar's title, particularly within the context of open worlds, it will be impossible for it to escape associations with future representatives of the genre, who will undoubtedly seek to learn from it.

Although comparisons are generally odious, it's also true that they constitute a timely method to contrast the evolution, or involution, of a medium, so I can already see many scholars of this art revisiting its confines to diagnose its eventual state.

While I acknowledge the omnipresence of the internet and our hyper-connected state has made the task of hunting for secrets virtually impossible, I know I'm not the only one who has deliberately avoided all discussion about the game in order to discover it for myself.

By choosing not to use guides, watch gameplay videos, or even compare opinions, the game's lifespan is instantly extended due to its immeasurable size and content, much of which is hidden behind hundreds of hours of spontaneous and meticulous exploration.

You may finish the campaign and feel satisfied with what you've experienced, but for a game that has taken so long to arrive and generated so much anticipation, I'm sure that a large portion of its player base will continue playing until there's no dialogue, NPC, mission, weapon, or random event left undiscovered.

This largely depends on how much you choose to interact with its online discourse, as you will surely encounter spoilers of all kinds as the days and months go by, yet a whole second life awaits you if you choose to turn a blind eye to other people's experiences and strive to discover everything on your own.

Assuming I'm not the only oddball who's spent countless hours wandering around open-world games listening to their tunes without engaging in any particular activity, GTA 6's deep and outstanding soundtrack will behave like a music player with extra steps.

In fact, a large part of my GTA 5 playtime consisted of countless nights spent hopping into any legitimately acquired vehicle and cruising around the city's interiors and exteriors, and after just an hour of playing this new installment, I already knew the future would be the same.

Whether you enjoy pop, urban music, rap, or listening to the radio as if it were real life (which it is closer to than I'd like to admit), there's a station for every type of listener, helping the game also become an album that will remind you of the era in which it was released.

Never underestimate the power of songs as tools to prolong our connection with a video game because, just like with Secunda in Skyrim or I Really Want To Stay at Your House in Cyberpunk 2077, I'm sure RHYNO will have us going around in circles in Vice City for a very, very long time.

Like many games, Grand Theft Auto 6 is full of easter eggs for you to discover. These are some of the best Leonida has to offer.

A major surprise I encountered in my first few hours of playing GTA 6 was the influence of immersive sims on its mission design, as there isn't just one way to solve many of the main and side objectives in the campaign.

Obviously, we're not talking about the depth of an Arkane Studios title, though there's enough density and player agency to allow for diverse approaches, ranging from peaceful resolutions if you know who to talk to, to stealthy sieges where no one necessarily has to be killed.

Add to that the game's inherent spontaneity, which throws you into special and unexpected encounters every second, all waiting to grab your attention, and you realize its replayability stems from a design specifically intended to be open and multifaceted.

I hope GTA 6's approach helps the genre emerge from its slumber, but while I invoke every possible deity to make that happen, I'm content to return to Leonida every few years to see what new interactions Rockstar prepared without me noticing in my first five playthroughs.

In conjunction with the above, the title places a notable emphasis on role-playing elements, influencing both the story and gameplay according to how the player chooses to interact with their world, allowing Jason and Lucia to be canvases with clear forms yet ultimately emphasized by the player.

Between choosing the type of relationship they develop, making choices that influence the narrative at key plot points, and the constant decision-making involved in adhering to (or not) morality and law, you can have completely different experiences if you shift your mindset enough.

In this sense, for my first playthrough, I have a more restrained and rigorous Jason and a more antisocial and rebellious Lucia within a loving relationship, always acting in accordance with these personality archetypes. Regardless, for my second playthrough, I plan to take a completely opposite path.

The result? At the very least, one more run with hundreds of hours and variations that will make me even more amazed by the immeasurable talent of the Rockstar workers, to whom I feel I owe the respect of playing the game at least three times to properly appreciate the countless hours they invested in shaping the product.

The third of my three planned playthroughs, designed to fully exploit the game, will consist of not killing anyone unless the game forces me to, which brings us to the mechanism that has kept hundreds of video games alive online: challenge runs.

Beating the entire game with only fists, without breaking any laws, without using money, with only a knife, using only public transport, in the shortest time feasible, as the worst possible partner... I don't know if the possibilities are truly infinite, but they certainly come close.

Games like Dark Souls and Hollow Knight have demonstrated for years that human creativity knows no bounds, especially when it comes to creating content that borders on masochism, so it's only natural that GTA 6 will be like a second home for all these inventive people.

I don't know if I'll be among them, yet my experience being chronically online assures me with complete certainty that GTA 6 will sustain entire communities based on challenges, rising exponentially if mods are added to the equation.

Some players may think they should register a hot new sports car as their starter car. There's actually a better choice. Here's the best starter car to register in GTA VI.

Heraclitus said it's impossible to step into the same river twice because everything changes, both in the river itself and in the person crossing it, and I believe the mythical Greek philosopher made this aphorism with the belief that we would eventually have the boundless body of water that is GTA 6.

Experiences with open worlds, like the aforementioned Skyrim or, more recently, Elden Ring, tend to be special thanks to the organic nature of their worlds, given you feel like you're in an alternate, digital reality where you're truly part of a larger cosmos.

Leonida, however, takes these sensations to uncharted territory, where it genuinely feels impossible to experience the same thing twice because of how reactive and multifaceted its systems are, like hundreds of thousands of windows that only open if you're in the right place at the right time.

This contextual fertility ensures that there will almost always be a new experience to go through, and as long as the flame of belief that there are unexplored horizons remains alive (something that GTA 5 already demonstrated), there will be parishioners who remain absorbed watching the fire, waiting to hear an unprecedented crackle.

The fear of missing out on a cultural event is fascinating because, contrary to popular belief, it can have a timeless quality; for example, it's the reason I played the first iterations of Red Dead Redemption and The Last of Us, even though it was a decade after their respective releases.

Given GTA 6 is and will be a cultural touchstone of modern entertainment, many will return to its realm years later to satisfy a curiosity they perhaps didn't solve at launch for one reason or another, ranging from waiting for a price drop to the complete optimization of its features.

Beyond the causes, and considering a legacy that is already titanic after just one week of release and will become even more staggering as time goes on, it seems that playing GTA 6 will be like watching The Godfather or reading the Odyssey: an essential ritual for understanding the path its medium will take in the future.

Even if you're not a fan of the series or the genre, the curiosity to understand the reasons behind its multi-million sales and resounding unanimous praise as a masterpiece on Metacritic will be compelling for those who value video games as an art form, since great works always deserve attention, even if it's to criticize them.

A very upset parrot is more than willing to point players in the direction of cash if they beat down its jailers.

Rockstar has found its closest model to follow in GTA 5, the same recipe that allowed them to maintain the product's relevance for over ten years with virtually no significant drop in popularity or impact, whose success hinges on spacing out re-releases, which will rekindle the unresolved desires of a significant portion of the gaming community.

Motivated by the release of the PC version and potential upcoming consoles from Microsoft and Sony, or even by the anticipation of a product with as few bugs and inconsistencies as possible, many people will refrain from jumping on the bandwagon at its peak, instead patiently waiting for the waters to calm down.

The 235 million copies sold of its predecessor didn't happen overnight; they materialized gradually and steadily year after year, and it's quite easy to predict that market behavior this time around will be virtually the same.

Many of them are repeat buyers, of course, but that doesn't invalidate the title's statement: whether it's your first time or your fiftieth, the hardware will give you very appealing reasons to discover or check out how GTA 6 is, even if it's 2036.

However, by far, the biggest reason to be sure you'll be playing GTA 6 for more than ten years lies in its multiplayer mode, a fundamental pillar that sustained GTA 5 throughout its lifespan and which, without a doubt, will repeat that feat with this new installment.

If we assume Rockstar will be able to create a product that surpasses its predecessor as the base game did, the only sensible conclusion about the next iteration of GTA Online is that it will be a candidate for the most massive, complex, and profitable multiplayer experience of all time.

Phenomena like Fortnite or League of Legends cast doubt on such a claim, but the fact that this is even the scale used to measure GTA 6's multiplayer is indicative enough of what it will mean for the franchise and the market once it's released.

More than the sheer scale of its world, more than sociocultural pressure, and more than even any traditional DLC, what could allow Rockstar to go two generations without releasing a game and still be the most popular developer in the world is the online variant of GTA 6.

Not only because of its name and legacy, which also mean a great deal, but because of the game's inherent quality, which suggests that its size, freedom of action, and overall quality will be remarkable enough to carry the Grand Theft Auto name for as long as it lasts.

Grand Theft Auto 6 puts a large emphasis on keeping your relationship sound, so you need to know what ways are the best to raise the romance between Jason and Lucia.

#4276. Peppermint oil significantly lowers blood pressure in just 20 days

Peppermint oil, best known for its refreshing flavor and soothing effects on digestion, may also offer a surprising benefit for people with mildly elevated blood pressure.

Researchers at the University of Lancashire found that consuming a small amount of peppermint oil each day for just 20 days significantly reduced systolic blood pressure (the top number in a blood pressure reading). Participants who received peppermint oil had systolic readings that were an average of 8.5 mmHg lower than those who received a placebo after accounting for their starting blood pressure.

The findings, published in the journal PLOS One, suggest that peppermint oil could provide a simple, inexpensive, and well-tolerated way to help manage mildly elevated blood pressure.

Lead author Dr. Jonnie Sinclair, Reader in Sport and Health Sciences, said: "High blood pressure is one of the biggest causes of heart disease and death worldwide, and it costs a huge amount of money to treat. Although medicines are commonly used to treat it, it's not always clear how well they work in the long-term, and they can cause unwanted side effects."

How Peppermint Oil May Lower Blood Pressure

Peppermint naturally contains several biologically active compounds, including menthol, which gives the plant its distinctive cooling sensation, and flavonoids, a group of plant compounds known for their antioxidant properties.

Peppermint also has anti-inflammatory and vasodilatory properties, meaning it may help blood vessels relax and widen. When blood vessels widen, blood can flow more easily, potentially reducing the pressure exerted against artery walls. These properties may help explain peppermint oil's effects on blood pressure, although the precise mechanisms require further investigation.

To examine these potential benefits, researchers recruited 40 adults between the ages of 18 and 65 with elevated blood pressure or stage 1 hypertension, an early stage of high blood pressure. Participants were randomly assigned to one of two groups.

One group consumed a total of 100 microliters of food-grade peppermint oil each day, equivalent to one-tenth of a milliliter, divided into two doses diluted in water. The other group received a peppermint-flavored placebo that contained none of the active peppermint oil compounds.

Significant Blood Pressure Improvements in Just 20 Days

After 20 days, average systolic blood pressure among participants taking peppermint oil fell from approximately 130 to 122 mmHg. Meanwhile, blood pressure remained virtually unchanged in the placebo group.

Systolic blood pressure measures the force of blood against artery walls when the heart contracts. Persistently elevated readings can damage blood vessels over time and increase the risk of serious health problems, including heart attacks, strokes, and heart failure.

Although systolic blood pressure was the primary focus of the study, researchers also examined body measurements, blood test results, diastolic blood pressure (the bottom number in a blood pressure reading), resting heart rate, mental well-being, and sleep quality.

A Promising, Low-Cost Approach to High Blood Pressure

Dr. Sinclair added: "Our findings were very positive and they have significant clinical implications, especially given arterial hypertension is the most common preventable risk factor for cardiometabolic disease and the greatest single risk factor for global mortality.

"Peppermint oil is low in calories and price so it's proved to be a very simple and cost-effective solution to potentially treat millions of people around the world."

While the results are encouraging, the study involved a relatively small number of participants and lasted less than three weeks. Larger and longer clinical trials will be needed to determine whether the benefits persist over time and whether peppermint oil could complement existing blood pressure treatments.

The researchers used peppermint oil specifically intended for human consumption. The findings should not be interpreted as a reason to replace prescribed blood pressure medications or ingest essential oils that are not formulated for oral use.

Materials provided by University of Lancashire. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

#4274. Stanford scientists discover 3 hidden brain types behind ADHD and anxiety

A new Stanford Medicine-led study has identified three distinct biological brain types, known as biotypes, in children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), anxiety disorder or both conditions.

The findings could help unravel the complicated relationship between two of the most common childhood mental health disorders, which frequently share symptoms. Published recently in Nature Mental Health, the study reveals that each biotype involves disruptions in a different set of brain circuits.

By examining thousands of functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) scans, researchers identified three biological patterns associated with different groups of symptoms. These findings could eventually help doctors recognize ADHD and anxiety earlier, identify new targets for treatment, and determine which therapies are most likely to benefit individual patients.

"The high overlap between ADHD and anxiety actually hinders our understanding of the neurobiology underlying traditional, symptom-based diagnoses," said co-senior study author Yu Zhang, PhD, assistant professor of psychiatry and behavioral sciences.

Doctors currently rely on symptom checklists to diagnose ADHD and anxiety. However, Zhang explained that children diagnosed with either disorder frequently experience symptoms associated with the other.

Looking Beyond Traditional ADHD and Anxiety Diagnoses

Yong Jiao, PhD, a postdoctoral scholar at the University of Iowa, is the study's lead author. Zhang shares senior authorship with Jing Jiang, PhD, assistant professor of pediatric neurology at the University of Iowa.

"We wanted to know whether the biological differences among children with ADHD and anxiety follow the diagnostic labels used in the clinic," Zhang said.

The researchers found that the relationship was not so straightforward. Children diagnosed with ADHD, anxiety or both could belong to any of the three brain biotypes, although some biological patterns were more prevalent among children with particular diagnoses.

According to the researchers, identifying these underlying differences could add a valuable layer of biological information to existing diagnostic categories, benefiting both future research and clinical care.

AI Uncovers Hidden Patterns in Thousands of Brain Scans

The research team drew on data from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development study, an ongoing investigation of brain development involving more than 11,000 children across the United States. Participants were 9 or 10 years old when they entered the project.

The analysis included 3,508 children who already had a diagnosis of ADHD, anxiety or both when they enrolled, along with 693 children who initially had neither diagnosis but subsequently developed one or both conditions. Another 1,947 children who never received either diagnosis served as a control group.

All participants underwent fMRI brain scans and completed a series of cognitive and behavioral assessments. To independently validate their findings, the scientists examined brain scans from another 224 children participating in a separate research project called the Healthy Brain Network. Each child in this additional group had been diagnosed with ADHD or anxiety disorder.

The team developed an artificial intelligence model to investigate functional connectivity, which describes how different regions of the brain work together. By incorporating diagnostic information and behavioral test results, the model identified patterns of brain connectivity that were more pronounced in children with ADHD, anxiety or both compared with those who had neither condition.

Combining behavioral information with brain imaging data revealed two major dimensions of dysfunction associated with ADHD and anxiety: cognitive-behavioral dysfunction and emotion-attention dysfunction.

Each dimension involves a different network of brain regions. Different combinations of these disruptions produced three distinct biotypes, which the researchers named the externalizing-disinhibited biotype, the internalizing-distressed biotype and the mixed biotype.

Three Distinct Brain Types and Their Symptoms

The three biological categories were mutually exclusive (each child was in only one biotype), but none was limited to a particular traditional diagnosis.

Children belonging to the externalizing-disinhibited group tended to exhibit higher levels of impulsivity, hostility, defiance, aggression and rule-breaking behavior. ADHD diagnoses were more common among children in this group.

The internalizing-distressed group was characterized by greater feelings of guilt and tension, stronger perfectionist tendencies, and more symptoms associated with anxiety and depression. Children with this biological profile were more frequently diagnosed with anxiety disorders.

Those in the mixed group experienced more difficulties with attention, irritability and self-injury. Like children in the externalizing-disinhibited group, they were more likely to have an ADHD diagnosis.

Despite these tendencies, researchers found every combination of brain biotype and conventional diagnosis among the children they studied.

Brain Changes Could Reveal ADHD and Anxiety Before Diagnosis

One of the most surprising findings emerged when scientists examined brain scans taken from children who had not been diagnosed with ADHD or anxiety when they first entered the study.

The distinctive biological patterns were already detectable in their initial scans, even though the children did not receive a diagnosis of ADHD, anxiety or both until later.

"We think this means we may be able to use the biotypes as an early indicator of these conditions," Zhang said, noting that identifying these patterns before diagnosis was the most unexpected aspect of the research. "It could help us provide more timely intervention for these conditions and slow down or, we hope, even reverse their progression."

Toward More Personalized ADHD and Anxiety Treatments

Zhang does not expect the newly identified brain biotypes to replace conventional diagnoses based on symptoms. Instead, combining the two approaches could help clinicians select treatments that are better suited to individual children.

Finding an effective treatment for ADHD or anxiety currently involves considerable experimentation. Children may need to try several medications before discovering which one provides meaningful relief.

"When doctors prescribe a new medication, it can take quite a long time -- a couple of weeks or months -- to see a response," Zhang said. "If the first medication doesn't work, they switch to a different one"

This process can be lengthy, expensive and frustrating.

Zhang hopes future clinical trials will build on the team's findings by investigating how different treatments affect specific patterns of brain activity. Such studies could eventually help researchers determine which therapies are most effective for each of the three biotypes.

"We want to find biomarkers that can really inform the right treatment at the right time," he said.

Researchers involved in the study are affiliated with Stanford University's Wu Tsai Neurosciences Institute and the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered AI.

Additional contributors came from the University of Iowa, the University of Texas at Austin and the University of Pennsylvania Perelman School of Medicine.

The research received funding from the National Institutes of Health (grant numbers R01MH129694, R01MH136197, R01MH145082, R01MH140425, U24AA021697, R01DA057567, R37MH101495 and R01MH132784), the Eagles Autism Foundation, the Stanford Knight Initiative for Brain Resilience, the Rosenkranz Foundation, the Brain and Behavior Research Foundation, and the Effie and Wofford Cain Foundation.

#4273. Nongshim RedForce sign Deft after military service, reuniting DRX’s 2022 world title trio

Nongshim RedForce have brought 2022 world champion Deft back to the LCK and paired him again with Kingen and Pyosik. The move follows an eighth-place 2026 for the club and comes days after BLG ended Korea's four-year hold on the World Championship.

Kim ‘Deft’ Hyuk-kyu’s signing was confirmed on 19 November. The club used its official social media channels to make the announcement. Deft began his military service after the 2024 season ended.

The deal reunites him with two members of the DRX side that won the 2022 World Championship. Jungler Hong ‘Pyosik’ Chang-hyeon joined later the same day, alongside support Moon ‘Andil’ Gwan-bin. Top laner Hwang ‘Kingen’ Seong-hoon had re-signed a day earlier.

Deft’s signing was announced at 7pm. The Pyosik and Andil additions that followed completed Nongshim’s five-man starting line-up, Inven Global reported. Mid laner Seon ‘Calix’ Hyeon-bin provides continuity. He has been with the organisation since 2021 and extended his deal on 18 November.

Deft brings a long winning record. He made his debut with MVP Blue in 2013. His titles include the LCK, the LPL, the Mid-Season Invitational and the 2022 World Championship.

Kingen first joined Nongshim for the 2025 season. Pyosik arrives after a difficult 2026 at DN SOOPers. That team lost a run of matches, and rookie Sharvel took his starting place.

The move had been signalled. About a month before the announcement, Sheep Esports reported from Korean sources that Nongshim planned to sign Deft. The same report said rookie AD carry Diable would need a new team.

The signings mark a sharp change of direction after a poor year. Once the league campaign was over, the team lasted just a single match in the play-ins.

The deal lands days after a setback for the whole league. Bilibili Gaming’s victory over Gen.G came at the Barclays Center in New York. It gave the organisation its first Summoner’s Cup.

BLG won all four of its series against LCK teams at the tournament. Every LCK seed fell to the Chinese side on its way to the trophy. The title is also the LPL’s first since EDward Gaming won in 2021.

'Deft' has signed a contract as the new ADC of NS RedForce LCK Team.

Please look forward to and support Deft, who has written new history with an unbreakable spirit through countless trials, as he takes on new challenges and delivers great… pic.twitter.com/bHa1uJWwKV

— NS RedForce (@NS_RedForce) November 19, 2026

For Nongshim, a line-up built around three 2022 champions now has an international calendar to aim at. Riot Games has moved First Stand 2027 from Southeast Asia to China and renamed it First Stand: All In. It will be a one-off expanded edition with more teams and players.

Spain gets its debut as a Mid-Season Invitational host in 2027, with Valencia’s Feria de Valencia as the venue. Before that, Riot plans to publish First Stand: All In’s format and qualification process in January.

#4272. 8 Reasons Jason and Lucia’s Relationship is Better Than Yours

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

Do you think you have a good relationship? Do you and your partner get along, and are you both happy? Do you have trust, and are you both still making each other laugh? If you are iffy on any of those questions, Lucia and Jason may just have a better relationship than you.

Grand Theft Auto 6 puts a big emphasis on the relationship between Jason and Lucia, with it being a key part of the story. From the very start of the game, you need to put them first if you want them to have a strong connection.

Well, their relationship is good. They can trust each other, and they will put their lives on the line to keep one another safe. Can you say the same?

A key part of learning about your partner is asking them questions. You need to have a sense of interest in your significant other so that they know you truly love them. Without any type of interest, you end up becoming stale.

That is not a problem for Lucia and Jason, as they ask each other questions all the time. If you simply drive around the city, you will hear conversations between the two of them where Lucia will ask Jason how he ended up in the military.

You will also hear Jason ask Lucia about her past, about prison, and about their son. This interest shows how much they care about each other and want to know more about one another.

Trust is a key part of any relationship. If you don’t trust the person you are with, odds are you won’t make it very long. It is one of the most core tenets of any relationship, and Jason and Lucia show that they can trust each other constantly.

They put their lives on the line every time they step out of their apartment. They are constantly dealing with drug lords, gang members, and more, so they need someone they can trust, and they can trust each other.

Both of them know that the other one has their back, and when one of them makes a strong move, the other is there to back them up.

The internet made a huge stink about not being able to cheat on Lucia as Jason. Many people kept saying they wanted to see what a relationship with Mandy would be like. It would probably be terrible, but they were interested.

However, the game not having a cheat mechanic in it just shows the strength of Jason and Lucia’s relationship. You can’t betray Lucia. You can’t go behind her back. You are required to stay loyal, but that is also the kind of guy Jason is.

Jason wouldn’t go behind someone’s back, no, he is too good for that. He is the type of guy who would rather break it off if things weren’t going right than go behind someone’s back.

GTA 6 removes the ability solicit, a GTA feature since 2001. Rockstar says the decision supports Jason and Lucia’s story.

If you want to get to know your partner, and you want to have a solid foundation, you need to spend quality time together doing things that you both enjoy. This can be a hobby like bowling, mini-golfing, or maybe even robbing banks.

For Jason and Lucia, you have the option to have them spend time together constantly. They are able to go for walks around Vice City, take a drive, or participate in any of the various side activities found throughout the game.

This type of constant quality time is great for a relationship, and it is okay to spend time apart. After all, you can split up from each other in the game, but the quality time is there, and it builds their relationship.

Communication is everything when it comes to being in a relationship. You don’t want to keep secrets, and you always want to check in to make sure that your partner is okay. This style of communication is key to making things work.

Jason and Lucia are a model example of this. When playing as either of them, you have the option to check in with the other to see how they are doing. Your partner will also sometimes send you a text or give you a call to check in.

This type of relationship works because they keep a constant line of communication. They share group chats, and they also talk about what happened when they were split up.

Let's face it, in GTA 6, Lucia is not the greatest role model. In fact, she has some major red flags.

While it isn’t necessary for you and your partner to have the same exact goals in life, it certainly does help to make things operate more smoothly. For instance, if you don’t want kids but your partner does, that can cause a rift.

Jason and Lucia don’t need to worry about this rift forming as they know exactly why they are doing what they are doing, and they have the same goals. They both want to provide for their child, and they don’t want to be criminals forever.

They are criminals now to get enough money to live a good life later on. After that, they don’t need to keep going, as they will be able to live happily as a family.

A nice thing about being in a relationship is that you have somebody you can connect with - somebody that can make you smile, laugh, and feel a range of emotions. To keep things going well, you need to keep up the humor, you need to be flirty, and you need to be playful.

The relationship between Lucia and Jason in GTA 6 isn’t stale. They are consistently making each other laugh, flirting with one another, and more. They know how to make each other smile.

You can complete a job, and the two of them will joke about something, or you can make it back to the apartment, and they will be intimate. You can also relax in bed staring at your phone. There is a connection, and it is strong.

This doesn’t apply to everyone. After all, not many couples out there are actively committing crime together and bailing each other out. Jason and Lucia have a bond that is forged in fire and a hailstorm of bullets. I wish I was joking.

Their relationship may seem okay at first, but once you are out of chapter one, you see how Lucia goes the extra mile for Jason. She puts her life on the line for him, and he does the same in return.

The two are willing to die for each other if it means that their partner stays safe. Those aren’t just words to them. Each time they go out, they are risking their lives for each other, and it shows how madly in love they are.

Grand Theft Auto 6 puts a large emphasis on keeping your relationship sound, so you need to know what ways are the best to raise the romance between Jason and Lucia.

#4271. The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – November 13, 2026

Today is Friday the 13th, but let's not dwell on that. Here are some weekend video games to play. Well, actually, here are some of our biggest stories of the week, and then you can check out some weekend game recommendations.

Also, go ahead and make some space on your Xbox or PlayStation hard drive to make room for GTAVI. It's going to be about 200 GB and you can pre-load it now. Delete those games you're not going to return to. Delete all those video clips you'll never watch from every time you get a Trophy on your PlayStation. And you know what? Go ahead and delete Fortnite, too. It's time.

Calling all sickos of The Rootrees Are Dead, Return of the Obra Dinn, The Incident At Galley House, and everything in between: there’s another good deduction game to obsess over. Funeral for the Sun stars a historian who visits an abandoned Latin American town to piece together its turbulent history, chiefly the truth behind the mysterious disappearance of its hundreds of residents (who were, officially speaking, lost in a fire). Supernatural forces allow players to peer into the town’s past to learn about key people potentially responsible for the calamity, who they must identify by name, establish relationships between, and even match younger and older versions of themselves. You even keep track of information using a multi-function notebook à la The Roottrees Are Dead. Boasting an enticing story, a beautiful painterly art direction, and a tight runtime at roughly 8-hours (or less if you’re really on a roll), Funeral for the Sun is a mystery worth unraveling if you need a new deduction game to cozy up with.

NetEase has continued to impress with the pace and quality of its regular updates to Marvel Rivals, which continues today with the release of an 11th season for the superhero battler. Right here at launch, the notable addition is he arrival of X-Men hero Nightcrawler, who BAMFs his way into battle as a strategist, equally capable of healing allies and taking out foes with his sword and brimstone bombs. As is almost always the case right at a new hero’s launch, it can be hard to snag him on the roster on opening day to see how he plays, but once you do, I expect you’ll find him a versatile healer who can pretty dramatically shake up the battlefield, especially with his Ultimate, which basically consolidates allies and enemies together in one central clump for a frenzied exchange of blows. Alongside the new batch of seasonal cosmetics and events to dive into, it’s once again a good time to don your hero outfit and take on some matches.

Pikmin 4 released on Switch 2 this week (or upgraded to Switch 2 depending on how you look at it), and that's a good thing. Pikmin 4 is the best game in the series and the Switch 2 version is the best version. That's great for those who never finished the game (your save does transfer) or skipped Pikmin 4 when it released in 2023, but if you're looking for an excuse to return to the game and play new content, the Dandori Academy addition is underwhelming. You can read my full thoughts here.

Metaphor: ReFantazio, originally released in 2024, is a great RPG from the creators of Persona. And the Persona lineage is obvious throughout the full game. You have to pick and choose where and with whom you should be spending your time, all while a big world-saving RPG with a memorable party of characters plays out in the foreground.

It released this week for Switch 2 and it’s a game that I think would play well on a handheld device. It’s also just a good RPG to play if you missed it previously.

Fun fact: Metaphor: ReFantazio was the game we had lined up to be the next cover when we were temporarily shut down in in 2024. We went to the studio and had a cover drawn up and everything. You can read the full details of the cover story that never was right here.

You can also read Game Informer's review of Metaphor: ReFantazio by following the link.

As we enjoy the final week in a pre-GTA VI world, what better way to gird your loins for next week’s release, so to speak, than by revisiting the last adventures set in Rockstar’s take on Miami? 2002’s Grand Theft Auto: Vice City is a certified classic that, if you’ve never played it, offers nice foundational insight into what Vice City was like in the ’80s (spoiler: it was a lot like Scarface and Miami Vice). Best of all, Vice City is easily available on current platforms with modernized improvements to boot.

If you want to go even further back, chronologically speaking, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories is a prequel set two years before the events of Vice City. Maybe, in some extremely minute way, Vice City Stories lays narrative groundwork for GTA VI. It’s unlikely, but you never know. Originally released for PSP in 2006, Vice City Stories is trickier to play if you don’t own Sony's retired handheld or a PlayStation 2, which it was ported to in 2007. But if you can find the means, there’s no better time to check out this often overlooked chapter of Vice City’s history.

I usually hold off on early access games, to preserve my experience for the finished product, but I just couldn’t resist Slay the Spire 2. The co-op gameplay is an awesome, major change, but even just adding a couple of new characters and cards would have satisfied my cravings. To that end, this week’s free update adds a brand new character, the Fool, who I’m eager to test out.

FYI, this new character is only available on the game’s beta, so you’ll have to go into the game settings on steam, click Properties, then Game Versions & Betas, and then opt into the “public-beta” version of the game to check the new content out. The patch notes for this update specifically say, “We expect to make a great number of content and balance changes before the Fool is ready for the main branch,” so expect frequent tweaks and a bit of a wait before the Fool joins the main Early Access branch. The new beta update also adds two more game modes: Dread and Blitz, which drastically alter your runs. If you want to wait a little while, the team at Mega Crit will refine these options into a more final form. But if you’re like me, more Slay the Spire 2 is more Slay the Spire 2, and I’m hopping in as soon as I can.

Monster Train 2 was one of my favorite games of last year, so I’m always glad to have a reason to jump back in. This week’s DLC, The Punished, is a perfect opportunity to do so, adding a new clan to the base game’s already packed roster. Since any clan can be combined with a second one to start a run, adding just one more option at the game’s start has an exponential effect, expanding the ways you can approach each attempt. As the DLC’s name implies, the new Punished clan gains buffs when taking damage, and you get new suite of cards that damages the whole playing field at once, harming foes and bolstering your allies. Even if you’re not checking out the DLC, the base game is absolutely worth picking up – just read my glowing review.

If you’ve been hankering for a new direction to go with your tabletop RPG group, may I recommend the incredibly versatile Cypher System from Monte Cook Games? The new Character Rulebook includes everything you need to get started, and set your adventures in virtually any fictional backdrop you can imagine, from hard sci-fi to gritty horror to high fantasy. Cypher’s polished approach to narrative-first and player-focused game sessions is much easier to pick up than many new rules systems, but it has enormous flexibility to deliver smart, creative, and exciting adventures that can help to change things up if your playing group has been in a rut.

#4270. Too much of this common nutrient could be accelerating blood vessel aging

Blood vessels naturally become less flexible with age, and certain diseases can accelerate this process. As blood vessels stiffen, the risk of cardiovascular disease and premature death increases.

One factor that can contribute to this damage is an excess of phosphate in the bloodstream. Although elevated blood phosphate (hyperphosphatemia) is relatively uncommon in the general population, it occurs much more frequently in people with chronic kidney disease (CKD), whose kidneys gradually lose their ability to filter waste from the blood.

Scientists at the University of Colorado Anschutz School of Medicine have identified a kidney protein that plays a critical role in regulating blood phosphate levels. The discovery could have particularly important implications for people living with CKD.

In a new study published in October 2026, the researchers found that a deficiency of this protein caused blood vessels to stiffen more rapidly and shortened lifespan in animal models. These effects were especially pronounced when the animals consumed a diet high in phosphate. Reducing phosphate intake helped alleviate some of the damage.

The findings point to a potential new target for medications and other therapies designed to maintain healthy phosphate levels. Such treatments could eventually help people with CKD improve their overall health and potentially live longer.

"Phosphate is really underestimated in terms of longevity in all mammals. The higher the concentration of phosphate in the blood, the shorter the lifespan," says Makoto Miyazaki, PhD, a research professor in the Division of Renal Diseases and Hypertension and the senior author of the new study.

How Excess Phosphate Accelerates Blood Vessel Aging

Phosphorus is an essential nutrient that helps build and maintain strong bones. It occurs naturally in a wide variety of whole foods, including meat, poultry, fish, whole grains, nuts, legumes, and dairy products, generally in the form of organic phosphate compounds. Food manufacturers also add phosphates to processed foods and beverages to improve flavor and extend shelf life.

Although phosphorus is necessary for good health, excessive levels in the blood (hyperphosphatemia) can trigger a series of damaging biological changes. Phosphate additives may be particularly concerning because the body absorbs them more rapidly and efficiently than the organic phosphates naturally present in whole foods.

Persistently elevated phosphate levels can cause smooth muscle cells within blood vessel walls to behave more like cells responsible for building bone. As a result, these cells begin depositing calcium phosphate crystals resembling those found in bones, causing the blood vessels to harden (or calcify).

Healthy blood vessels are flexible, allowing them to expand and contract in response to changing blood flow demands. Calcification compromises this flexibility, effectively accelerating vascular aging and potentially contributing to numerous age-related health problems throughout the body.

A Hidden Protein Helps Maintain Phosphate Balance

Under normal circumstances, the kidneys remove excess phosphate from the bloodstream before it reaches harmful levels. As CKD progresses, however, declining kidney function makes it increasingly difficult for the body to eliminate phosphate and other substances.

Maintaining the right amount of phosphate requires continuous adjustments. After the kidneys filter phosphate from the blood, a portion is eliminated through urine, while the remainder is returned to the circulation. A protein known as NPT2A is responsible for reabsorbing approximately 75% of the filtered phosphate, preventing the body from losing too much phosphorus.

When phosphate levels are already elevated, however, this recycling mechanism can become problematic. Miyazaki and his colleagues discovered that another protein, called TMEM174, acts as a natural brake on this process. By binding to NPT2A, it limits the amount of phosphate being reabsorbed into the bloodstream.

Protein Deficiency Shortens Lifespan in Animal Models

The latest findings highlight the importance of TMEM174 in maintaining healthy phosphate levels. Animals deficient in the protein struggled to regulate phosphate in their blood, experienced increased vascular calcification, and had significantly shorter lifespans.

"We don't fully understand how yet, but somehow TMEM174 is destabilizing NPT2A," says Miyazaki. "And without enough TMEM174, homeostasis is disrupted."

A deficiency of TMEM174 appears to result primarily from genetic factors rather than chronic kidney disease itself. However, the research suggests that people with CKD who also have insufficient levels of this protein could be particularly vulnerable to the harmful effects of excess phosphate.

A Potential New Target for Protecting Blood Vessels

Miyazaki hopes the discovery will lead to treatments that reduce the amount of excess phosphate the kidneys return to the bloodstream.

Dietary changes may provide some benefit, particularly by reducing consumption of fast food, deli meats, sodas, and other processed products that contain large amounts of phosphate. However, Miyazaki explains that managing phosphate levels through diet alone can be challenging, especially for people with CKD. Because phosphate is present in such a wide range of foods, avoiding it is virtually impossible.

In future research, Miyazaki plans to investigate these kidney proteins further, along with the hormones involved in maintaining the body's chemical balance. He also wants to better understand why calcium accumulation in blood vessels is so common among people with CKD.

For now, identifying the role of TMEM174 represents an important advance in understanding how the body regulates phosphate. It could also help lay the groundwork for new approaches to improving the health of people whose phosphate balance is disrupted.

"Scientists have been studying phosphate homeostasis for over 100 years, so to still find a new protein that regulates phosphate is kind of unique," says Miyazaki.

Materials provided by University of Colorado School of Medicine. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

#4268. 10 Elements Metroidvanias Could Borrow From GTA 6

Ronald is a video game journalist with more than 10 years of experience in the industry, working on several of the most important Spanish websites.

As someone who usually writes about Metroidvanias but has recently been engrossed in GTA 6, I haven't stopped thinking about the points where the two converge.

Rockstar's new work isn't an adventure like the series' previous iterations; instead, it boasts an even finer and more meticulous design that, at fleeting moments, makes me feel it hides lessons beyond the obvious.

That games in its genre will follow in its footsteps is logical, but I truly believe there's a sufficiently diverse level of excellence to consider that not only open-world titles will benefit from its influence.

Therefore, in order to return to writing about the type of games I'm passionate about while still fulfilling my communicative responsibility towards the interactive entertainment industry's latest titan, here are ten elements Metroidvanias could borrow from GTA 6.

Throughout its history, Grand Theft Auto has been a franchise of journeys, stories, and mechanics that unfold along the way rather than at the destination, giving vehicles a prominent role as in GTA 6.

In contrast, movement in Metroidvanias, despite the notable importance of exploration, is reduced to the characters and their abilities, limiting the worlds' scale to the equally slow speed at which their protagonists move.

Therefore, as the final stages of each campaign approach, fast travel becomes the key to backtracking, so the presence of manually controllable means of transport would not only add another layer of depth but also enable even larger worlds.

It doesn't have to be permanent, of course, as I personally love concrete maps that you can traverse on foot, yet the genre would benefit from a broader understanding of distance than it has been done so far.

Although I don't believe every game should have a plethora of minigames and side activities like GTA 6, I do think they highlight the narrow imagination with which Metroidvanias approach their gameplay concepts.

Speaking of verbs, fighting and moving are the only ones that can be attributed to their vast majority, instead of including more interactive elements that would help diversify the gaming experience.

Silver Pines, for example, does an excellent job in this regard by inheriting puzzles from horror games, but visual novels' decision-making, RPGs' morality systems, or stealth games' infiltrative sections could have a place in the right products.

Of course, it's easier to have diverse gameplay if you're an open-world game than if you're an action-adventure title, since the classification limits you, though I think it's a good time to break free from the shackles of labels.

Discover the best gym workouts in GTA 6, exercises to avoid, and how water and protein help you get more from your training.

Especially since FromSoftware's games have influenced the genre, it's become increasingly difficult to find a Metroidvania with a concrete story, told linearly and directly rather than through contextual and ambiguous elements.

These are rich and fertile narrative mechanisms for creating immersive worlds, no doubt, but the trope easily becomes exhausted after practically everyone resorts to it to tell their tales.

I'm not necessarily talking about cinematics or actors with impressive performances, but about campaigns with concrete beginnings, developments, and endings, as Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown and Ori and the Blind Forest have already done.

These examples demonstrate that it's achievable, and if we dare to go further and adopt a love story as emotional and sensitive as Jason and Lucia's, all the better.

Returning to the premise of gameplay variety, Metroidvanias have failed to convey the influence of their environments beyond the visual, as our ways of interacting with different biomes remain virtually unchanged.

You don't usually dive into aquatic biomes, just as you don't climb mountainous areas or sink into swamps, because the way we orient ourselves in space tends to be the same regardless of that location's unique characteristics.

In contrast, GTA 6 does a superb job of differentiating each of its regions, with activities adapted to the physical attributes of each one to truly convey the feeling that the world you're inhabiting exists.

I'm not suggesting the same level of depth or technological detail, but rather the same approach: to turn aesthetic beauty into playable immersion.

Find a fighter jet in GTA 6, learn how to enter Mile Zero Air Station, and escape the five-star wanted level after stealing one.

GTA 6, with its massive wardrobe and extensive customization system, reminded me of how special it felt to see Alucard's simple cape color change in Castlevania: Symphony of the Night depending on his equipment.

When you think of the greatest Metroidvanias, we all know and play the same protagonist, from their visual presentation to their gameplay styles, as the options are kept to a minimum to ensure precision and refinement.

It's a perfectly valid design sacrifice, and it has given us countless masterpieces, yet invalidating player expression by not allowing them to create their own unique gameplay and aesthetic combinations is a debt that has gone unpaid for years.

It's easier said than done, considering how much more difficult it is to conceive of an avatar that offers so many alternatives, but it's so captivating in GTA 6 that I can't help but dream with the possibility.

Even with the perpetual satire and exaggeration inherent in GTA 6's story, it reminded me how unusual realistic narratives have become within the video game industry, which is at the mercy of various forms of fantasy instead.

Thus, would playing a Metroidvania governed by our universal laws be even remotely as entertaining as one with an entirely new world? I don't have the slightest idea, precisely because this approach is so unexplored within the genre.

The conversations between Jason and Lucia feel so human, as do many of the events with NPCs and secondary characters, that you empathize almost instinctively, leading to a level of connection unusual in Metroidvanias.

Works like Shadow Complex or, to a lesser extent, Silver Pines itself, partially demonstrate this possibility, and I feel that exploring it would help open up a completely unique avenue for the genre, one that isn't limited to hand-drawn 2D side-scrollers.

Find a tank at Mile Zero Air Station in GTA 6. Learn where to enter the base, where the tanks are parked, and what to expect when you escape.

Among the most striking aspects of GTA 6 is the way every NPC reacts to your every move. Whether it's walking, wearing unusual clothing, drawing a weapon, or saying something, there's an interaction waiting for you around every corner.

In the context of Metroidvanias, games like Hollow Knight have already explored the idea of characters responding to our actions, and even with the system's restrictions, it's an integral element of its worldbuilding.

Accordingly, building on that foundation and with an eye on Leonida's organic world, campaigns can be created where we feel our influence isn't rigidly predetermined but rather gradually constructed on both a macro and micro level.

It's difficult to anticipate the rapid arrival of a structure with such ramifications due to the predominance of independent developers in the genre, though simply having the horizon in sight is enough to begin moving towards it.

Ever since I played The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim, I've realized that progression in video games is almost always extradiegetic—that is, it happens before the player's eyes, not so much the character's—and GTA 6 also rejected this principle.

Consequently, "finding" a skill instead of developing it is a statement in itself about how a character grows, which is quite functional for the Metroidvania philosophy but not so much for the feeling of evolving through our gameplay experience.

I doubt it's interesting to lock the double jump behind having to go to the gym and do jumping jacks for a whole week, yet a game where our combat and movement skills expand based on how we interact with its base mechanics is a future that excites me.

GTA 6 makes it very simple, and sometimes it's even annoying, but the fact that it works here for the sake of realism doesn't mean that Metroidvanias can't use the same methodology for the sake of fun.

In Metroidvanias, there's no such thing as approaches: you either play the way the game wants you to, or you simply have to give up on the possibility of finishing it altogether.

GTA 6, inevitably, is also a slave to determinism, yet it leans slightly towards immersive sim design, allowing you to choose how you're going to fulfill your unchangeable obligations.

There are fights you can avoid with dialogue, wars you can replace with stealthy takedowns, and conflicts you can relocate with distraction tactics, thanks in part to a level design that offers more than one way to handle its execution.

I would never ask a Metroidvania to be Dishonored, though I could respectfully request that it at least try to integrate the possibility that not every challenge is solved by depleting a boss's health bar or completing an artificial platforming challenge.

I'd be lying if I didn't say I'm quite a fan of the true ending trope hidden behind an obscure side mission that unfolds outside the main campaign, but it does sadden me that it's the only option Metroidvanias often display.

While GTA 6 emphasizes numerous decisions, circumstances, and systems that occur at pivotal points in the plot and throughout the game, Metroidvanias have a much more reductive model.

Regardless of how you play, games in this genre tend to follow the formula of "good ending, bad ending by changing a decision before the final boss, true ending behind an optional mission", and it's starting to lose its appeal.

Certainly, GTA 6's approach isn't necessarily revolutionary or life-changing, yet it's complex enough to make you think about how you interact with its systems, so it more than achieves its goal.

Of course, for there to be impactful decisions to make, it's necessary to apply several of the fundamentals mentioned in this list, as they can't be achieved in isolation. However, since Rockstar's game will surely be the benchmark for many years to come, I'm sure some lessons will sink in.

Grand Theft Auto 6 puts a large emphasis on keeping your relationship sound, so you need to know what ways are the best to raise the romance between Jason and Lucia.

#4267. Common sleep and anxiety drugs could be harming aging brains

Adults age 65 and older who have dementia or other cognitive disorders are particularly vulnerable to the harmful effects of medications used to treat anxiety, sleep disturbances, psychosis, and other conditions affecting the central nervous system.

Potential consequences include more emergency room visits, longer and more frequent hospital stays, declining mental health, and an increased risk of premature death.

New research from the University at Buffalo (UB) offers some encouraging news, however. Between 2011 and 2022, the proportion of older adults with cognitive disorders taking medications that could impair their cognitive function decreased significantly.

After analyzing data from 2,796 older adults with cognitive disorders who lived independently, researchers found that exposure to potentially inappropriate medications fell from 39.3% in 2011 to 29.3% in 2022.

"This is a population with some mental issues that relate to the central nervous system. These drugs also act on the central nervous system, so they can be too much for older adults if inappropriately used," says Haowen Hsu, PharmD, a postdoctoral fellow in the Department of Pharmacy Practice at the School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences and first author of the study, published in the Journal of the American Geriatrics Society.

Reducing the Risks of Common Prescription Drugs

Older adults who have spent years taking benzodiazepines such as Xanax for anxiety or sleep medications such as Ambien may benefit from a medically supervised reduction in dosage or gradual discontinuation. These medications can negatively affect cognitive function, balance, and coordination.

"A central word for patients in this age group is 'deprescribing,' which means, for example, removing inappropriate medications and decreasing the frequency or the dosage. In some cases, it means replacing the current medication with a milder alternative," Hsu says. "This is why it's so important for health care providers to work closely with community pharmacists and homecare nurses to optimize medication safety."

To identify potentially problematic drugs, the research team consulted the American Geriatrics Society's Beers Criteria, which identifies approximately 100 medications that may pose risks to older adults. The researchers then concentrated specifically on medications that could present additional dangers for people with diagnosed cognitive disorders.

Using data from the Medical Expenditure Panel Survey, the team examined a sample representing approximately 29.7 million older Americans with cognitive disorders over the period from 2011 to 2022. They compared individuals prescribed at least one potentially inappropriate medication with those who had not received any of these drugs.

Medication Safety Has Improved, but Risks Remain

Although the study did not examine what caused the decline in exposure to potentially harmful medications, Hsu points to growing awareness among researchers and clinicians over the past two decades. The gradual but sustained improvement may reflect broader advances in geriatric medicine and efforts to make prescription drug use safer.

"We were happy to see the percentages of harm decline over that 11-year period," he says. "However, one-third of our target population is still exposed to these harmful medications, which isn't good."

Older adults, even those without cognitive disorders, are particularly susceptible to harmful drug interactions and inappropriate prescriptions. In some cases, these complications can increase the risk of death. These dangers are a central focus of Team Alice, an ongoing interdisciplinary research initiative at the University at Buffalo dedicated to medication safety.

Team Alice takes its name from Alice Brennan, who died in 2009 following a prescription for a muscle relaxant identified as potentially inappropriate under the Beers Criteria. The prescribing error went unrecognized within the health care system, and Brennan died following six weeks of preventable complications.

Her daughter, Mary Brennan-Taylor, shared her mother's experience with University at Buffalo researchers in the hope of bringing about systemic changes that would spare other patients and families from similar harm.

Hsu began the new study shortly after joining the university's pharmacy school and Team Alice, where he works in the UB Patient Safety Learning Laboratory.

"This work extends a series of national analyses our group has published on potentially inappropriate medications, quality of life, and health care use in older adults," says David Jacobs, PharmD, PhD, associate professor of pharmacy practice and a principal investigator on Team Alice.

"It is especially important as older adults with cognitive disorders are the least able to tolerate medications that worsen memory or thinking, yet nearly one in three are still receiving them. Most of these patients have a regular source of care so these medications can be identified and addressed with their care team."

Improving Medication Safety for Older Adults

Other contributors to the study included Team Alice's fellow principal investigators Ranjit Singh, MD, associate professor and interim chair of the Department of Family Medicine at UB's Jacobs School of Medicine and Biomedical Sciences, and Robert Wahler, PharmD, clinical associate professor of pharmacy practice.

Collin Clark, PharmD, clinical associate professor of pharmacy practice, and Steven Feuerstein, an information systems analyst at the Jacobs School, also contributed to the research.

The findings underscore the value of thorough medication reviews during routine outpatient appointments. The researchers also suggest incorporating clinical assessment tools such as the Drug Burden Index into acute and outpatient care. Such tools can help health care professionals assess the combined effects of medications that act on the central nervous system and potentially prevent avoidable complications.

Further research is needed to establish whether improving medication use can enhance quality of life and reduce hospital admissions and emergency room visits among older adults experiencing cognitive difficulties.

A Rapidly Aging Population Raises New Concerns

The findings arrive at a significant moment in global demographic history. According to a recent report from the U.S. Census Bureau, adults age 65 and older now outnumber children from birth through age 5 worldwide for the first time in human history.

However, greater longevity does not necessarily translate into more years of good health. The same report indicates that nearly 75% of adults age 65 and older have at least two chronic health conditions. Managing multiple illnesses often requires taking more medications, some of which may have detrimental effects on the aging body and brain.

"This is an issue that has been building for decades, but the growth of the older adult population has arrived sooner than we expected," Hsu says. "This means that health care professionals need to pay closer attention than ever to medication safety, especially for older adults experiencing cognitive decline or other complex health concerns."

#4264. Scientists discover a surprising twist in how the body burns calories

Unlike ordinary body fat, brown fat burns calories to generate heat, making it an attractive target for future obesity treatments. Researchers at the University of Basel and University Hospital Basel have now investigated whether medication can switch on this energy-burning tissue in humans. Their surprising findings suggest that harnessing brown fat with drugs may be more challenging than anticipated.

While white fat primarily serves as an energy reserve, brown adipose tissue uses energy to keep the body warm. People with more active brown fat also tend to be leaner and have better metabolic health.

Exposure to cold naturally activates brown fat, prompting scientists to search for medications that could mimic this response. A research team led by Professor Matthias Betz at the University of Basel and University Hospital Basel examined whether activating a specific receptor, known as the beta2 adrenergic receptor, could stimulate brown fat in humans. Their findings were published in the journal Cell Metabolism.

Drug Boosts Calorie Burning Without Clear Brown Fat Activation

To investigate, the researchers conducted two experiments involving 11 healthy volunteers. They compared the effects of mild cold exposure with those of fenoterol, a medication that stimulates beta2 adrenergic receptors. The scientists measured how much energy the participants expended and used PET/CT scans to monitor brown fat activity.

Both interventions caused the body to burn more energy. However, the scans revealed an important difference. Only cold exposure produced clear evidence of brown fat activation, with the tissue absorbing considerably more glucose than it did following fenoterol administration.

"We were surprised that energy expenditure increased strongly with fenoterol even though we could not detect a comparable activation of brown fat," says Betz. "Our study shows that an increase in energy expenditure does not automatically mean that brown fat has been activated."

Exactly where the additional energy is being consumed remains a mystery. The researchers suspect that fenoterol may increase energy consumption in other tissues, potentially including skeletal muscle or white fat.

Implications for Future Weight Loss Drugs

The findings also suggest that the biological mechanisms controlling brown fat in humans are more complex than previously thought. Analysis of human tissue indicates that fully activating brown fat may require the combined action of multiple receptors or biological signals rather than stimulating a single receptor.

Understanding these mechanisms could open new possibilities for treating obesity. Current weight loss medications work by reducing appetite. However, as people shed pounds, their bodies often compensate by burning fewer calories.

A treatment that simultaneously reduces appetite and increases calorie burning could help counteract this metabolic adaptation.

"Ideally, we could combine a reduction in appetite with an increase in energy expenditure," says Betz. "But first we need a better understanding of how brown adipose tissue is regulated."

#4261. GTA 6 Workers Union Survived Execs, But Drowned at the Shore

Rockstar Games has had an incredible week following the launch of GTA 6, but the same can't be said for the developers who were hoping to secure formal recognition for their union. The results of a ballot among Rockstar's UK employees are out, and roughly three-quarters of those who voted have rejected the proposed agreement with the Independent Workers' Union of Great Britain (IWGB).

Rockstar’s UK staff will vote on union recognition from November 12 to 26, with the voting period spanning GTA 6’s November 19 launch.

As VGC reports, the ballot had a high turnout among the roughly 1,600 eligible employees. Only 25% of votes were in favor of the deal. It's a disappointing outcome for the organizers, especially considering that they managed to get as far as negotiating an agreement with Rockstar after last year's controversial dismissals.

The ballot opened on November 12 and closed today, November 26. Had the vote gone the other way, Rockstar would have been home to the largest formally recognized union in the UK video game industry, according to the IWGB.

The negotiations weren't just about securing better salaries for GTA 6 developers. The proposed arrangement would have given staff a means of collectively negotiating everything from overtime compensation to pensions, as well as a say in how the company handles redundancies and the use of AI.

Rockstar had already said it would recognize the union if its staff wanted one. What makes today's outcome particularly striking is that the agreement didn't fall apart at the negotiating table. It was the vote among employees that ultimately put an end to it.

It was the vote among employees that ultimately put an end to it.

Speaking about the result, Rockstar's head of publishing, Jennifer Kolbe, said it demonstrated employees' preference for dealing directly with the company. The IWGB, meanwhile, acknowledged that it still needs to earn the confidence of more staff members.

That doesn't mean the Rockstar Game Workers Union has ceased to exist, nor does it mean that employees have lost their right to join it. The union can still represent its members, but Rockstar won't be bound by the formal bargaining arrangement that was put to a vote.

It's worth remembering how unlikely it might have seemed a year ago that Rockstar's union organizers would even get to hold this vote. In October 2025, the company dismissed dozens of employees in an incident that subsequently led to an employment tribunal in the UK.

The IWGB alleged that the staff were targeted because of their involvement in union organizing. Rockstar, on the other hand, maintained that the dismissals were related to the sharing of confidential information on Discord. Today's ballot result doesn't settle that dispute, and the tribunal's outcome is still pending.

The timing of the vote also makes for a rather odd contrast with what's been happening outside Rockstar's offices. GTA 6 accounted for more than half of active PS5 and Xbox players tracked by Circana on launch day, and the game has already brought in billions of dollars in retail sales.

For some developers, though, the question is what happens to their jobs now that the game they've spent years working on is finally out. Even the commercial success of a game as big as GTA 6 can't guarantee that there won't be redundancies further down the line. That was one of the issues the union wanted to address before the launch.

The IWGB says it intends to keep organizing at Rockstar despite the vote. Hundreds of employees backed recognition, so the organizers aren't starting from scratch. Convincing the rest of their colleagues, however, is going to be a considerably bigger task than getting Rockstar to agree to hold the ballot in the first place.

GTA 6 is on track to be one of the biggest games of all time, but developers at Rockstar Games still have worries about job security.

This batch of Grammy noms also has fewer recurring nominees than past years.
