#4231. Common supplements rival antibiotics in treating severe gum disease

A familiar dietary supplement combined with low-dose aspirin may offer an unexpected alternative to antibiotics for people with severe gum disease. In a year-long clinical trial, patients who received omega-3 and aspirin alongside conventional periodontal treatment experienced nearly identical clinical benefits to those who received antibiotics. Perhaps even more surprisingly, the improvements were still evident six months after supplementation ended.

The findings, published in the Journal of Periodontology, come from researchers affiliated with Albert Einstein Israelite Hospital, Guarulhos University (UNG), the University of Taubaté (UNITAU), and the Ribeirão Preto School of Dentistry at USP (FORP-USP) in Brazil, as well as Harvard University in the United States.

The study suggests that combining omega-3 with low-dose acetylsalicylic acid (ASA), better known as aspirin, could reduce the need for antibiotics in certain patients. The discovery is particularly timely given growing worldwide concerns about antibiotic resistance, which occurs when bacteria develop the ability to survive exposure to drugs designed to kill them.

Why Severe Gum Disease Is So Difficult To Treat

Researchers monitored 109 patients with advanced periodontitis over 12 months. Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease that develops when bacteria accumulate below the gumline, triggering an immune response that can gradually damage the tissues and bone that hold teeth in place. Without proper treatment, the disease can cause teeth to loosen and eventually fall out.

As periodontitis progresses, spaces known as periodontal pockets form between the teeth and gums. These pockets can become increasingly deep, making it difficult to remove harmful bacteria through ordinary brushing and flossing.

"Patients with severe disease have very deep pockets, which act as reservoirs for bacteria associated with the disease. It's a very challenging condition to treat," says dental surgeon Nídia Cristina Castro dos Santos, the first author of the study and a professor and researcher at Einstein.

The researchers randomly divided the participants into four treatment groups. Every patient received subgingival instrumentation, commonly referred to as scaling. This standard periodontal treatment involves removing bacterial deposits and hardened plaque from tooth surfaces beneath the gums. Each group also received a different complementary treatment.

Patients in the control group received inactive substitutes for the antibiotics, omega-3, and aspirin, supplied in capsules that looked identical to those containing the active treatments.

A second group received metronidazole and amoxicillin three times daily for 14 days. This combination of antibiotics has some of the strongest scientific evidence supporting its use as an additional treatment for severe periodontitis.

Participants in the third group took three grams of omega-3 each day, together with a daily dose of low-dose aspirin, for six months. The fourth group received both interventions, taking antibiotics for two weeks while following the six-month omega-3 and aspirin regimen.

The researchers assessed the patients' progress at three, six, and 12 months.

At the end of the study, approximately 58% of patients in the antibiotic group had reached the researchers' clinical treatment target, defined as having no more than four remaining deep periodontal pockets.

The omega-3 and aspirin group achieved an almost identical success rate of 57.7%. By comparison, only 23.1% of patients who underwent scaling and received placebos reached the same target. Interestingly, administering both antibiotics and the omega-3 and aspirin regimen together did not produce any additional benefits.

Although antibiotics can improve treatment outcomes in patients with particularly severe gum disease, they are not routinely necessary for everyone with periodontitis.

"The use of antibiotics isn't considered the gold standard of treatment. Although metronidazole and amoxicillin yield good results in the most severe cases, their use should be evaluated on a case-by-case basis due to risks related to bacterial resistance and possible adverse effects," says Castro dos Santos.

Helping the Body Naturally Resolve Inflammation

The findings build on earlier research into the potential role of omega-3 fatty acids in protecting oral health. In a previous investigation, also supported by FAPESP and published in Scientific Reports, scientists found that omega-3 supplementation reduced periodontal inflammation and bone loss in rats. The protective effects were particularly notable when supplementation was combined with physical exercise.

Although results from animal studies do not necessarily translate directly to humans, the earlier findings provided clues that omega-3 might help regulate the inflammatory processes that contribute to gum disease.

Omega-3 fatty acids are a group of fats found in foods such as oily fish and are widely available as dietary supplements. Beyond their nutritional importance, they serve as building blocks for certain molecules that help regulate inflammation.

Castro explains that omega-3 works differently from conventional anti-inflammatory medications. Instead of simply interfering with pathways that promote inflammation, omega-3 helps the body produce molecules involved in bringing inflammation to a natural conclusion and supporting tissue repair.

This process, known as the resolution of inflammation, is an active biological mechanism that helps the body return to normal after an immune response. In chronic inflammatory diseases such as periodontitis, inflammation can persist and contribute to ongoing tissue damage.

The researchers included low-dose aspirin because it can promote the formation of certain inflammation-resolving molecules. They suspected that combining aspirin with omega-3 could strengthen the body's ability to control the persistent inflammation associated with advanced gum disease.

The researchers had originally expected antibiotics and the omega-3 regimen to work best when administered together. Instead, the findings revealed that targeting inflammation could produce clinical improvements comparable to those achieved through antibiotic treatment.

"We imagined that the combination of antibiotics and omega-3 would be most effective in controlling periodontitis in these patients. We also believed that the results for the group that used omega-3 with ASA would be slightly lower than those for the antibiotic group. The result was surprising because the two therapies performed very similarly, paving the way for it to become a treatment option for these patients," says Castro.

Equally intriguing was how long the improvements lasted. Six months after patients stopped taking omega-3 and aspirin, their clinical outcomes remained similar to those observed when the treatment ended.

According to Castro, this persistence raises the possibility that adjusting the body's inflammatory response could have lasting therapeutic effects. However, scientists are still working to understand the biological mechanisms responsible.

A Potential Alternative Amid Rising Antibiotic Resistance

For dental surgeon Magda Feres, the study's lead author and a full professor at the Harvard School of Dental Medicine and the Graduate Program in Dentistry at UNG, targeting the body's inflammatory response could provide a valuable treatment option for certain patients.

"The combination of omega-3 and low-dose aspirin achieved clinical benefits comparable to those of the metronidazole and amoxicillin protocol, opening up a real alternative for those who can't take antibiotics, especially patients with allergies or intolerance to these medications," she says.

The potential to reduce antibiotic use has implications that extend well beyond dentistry. Antibiotic resistance ranks among the greatest threats to global public health, making it increasingly important to identify effective treatment strategies that do not depend on these medications.

"Demonstrating that it's possible to treat severe periodontitis by modulating the body's own response is new and relevant information that helps preserve antibiotics for when they are truly indispensable," says Feres.

More Research Is Needed Before Clinical Practice Changes

Despite the encouraging findings, the researchers caution that the results are not sufficient to justify an immediate change in how dentists treat severe periodontitis. The participants did not have other significant systemic or oral diseases, meaning the results may not apply equally to patients with additional health conditions.

Larger studies involving more diverse populations will be needed to validate the findings and determine which patients are most likely to benefit from each treatment strategy.

It is also important to recognize that omega-3 and aspirin were used alongside professional periodontal treatment, rather than as a substitute for it. Aspirin carries potential risks, including an increased risk of bleeding, and may not be appropriate for everyone.

Meanwhile, Feres and her colleagues are investigating how the different treatments affect the communities of bacteria living inside periodontal pockets. Early microbiological findings point to a decline in bacterial species associated with periodontal disease and an increase in microorganisms linked to healthier gums.

These ongoing investigations could help explain why targeting inflammation produced such promising results and whether the approach can reliably benefit a broader range of patients.

"It's an important step forward, but not the end of the story. Therefore, the message is one of cautious optimism: we have a promising, scientifically plausible alternative to antibiotics in select cases. Routine replacement will require more evidence," she concludes.

GodLike Esports opened their VCT Pacific Kickoff: South Asia – Qualifier 2027 playoff campaign with a 2-0 win over Trigger Point Esports on Monday 23 November 2026. GodLike took both maps of the best-of-three upper bracket quarter-final. Trigger Point Esports now drop into the lower bracket of the double-elimination format.

The playoffs are being held online by Riot Games and JioBLAST. Series in the bracket are played as best-of-three or best-of-five.

GodLike arrived in form. They reached the playoffs with an unbeaten 4-0 record in the open qualifier, VLR.gg reported. They shared joint first to fourth place in that event, which ran from 17 to 20 November. Trigger Point finished in the group placed fifth to eighth.

GodLike fielded Karam1L, Paradox and RvK from India, alongside sayoo from Indonesia and azyshaha from the Philippines. Sabyasachi ‘Antidote’ Bose is listed as head coach, with Samar as substitute. Trigger Point’s listed players are SangraM, WEELJACK and RaJ.

South Asian teams cannot qualify directly for Kickoff. The top two from the playoffs join the Oceania playoff winner and the Southeast Asia playoff runner-up in a four-team Last Chance Qualifier. Only its winner goes through to Kickoff in Bangkok, according to Dot Esports.

The stakes are high. Twelve teams will play at Kickoff, and the top three will qualify for Masters 1. The route stays narrow later in the season too. South Asia has no direct place at the Cups, with Cup 1 in Manila and Cup 2 in Tokyo. It sends two teams to an eight-team Pacific LCQ, and the winner takes the last Cup place.

The qualifier also has a new organiser. Riot picked JioBLAST to run the South Asia qualifiers instead of NODWIN Gaming, the previous organiser. Riot has not said why it made the change.

The UK interest lies with SIGN Esports. They beat Zexar Esports 2-0 in another upper bracket quarter-final. Russel ‘Russ’ Mendes joined SIGN Esports on 16 November 2026. He is the only player from the UK in the eight-team playoff field.

Russ was born in 1998 and is of Indian descent. He won the VALORANT Challengers 2025 South Asia Grand Final with Velocity Gaming on 13 July 2025, when they beat S8UL 3-1.

GodLike Esports and SIGN Esports both remain in the upper bracket, one defeat away from the lower bracket. Trigger Point Esports and Zexar Esports must win from the lower bracket to stay in contention for a top-two finish. The playoffs run until 29 November 2026.

Be it creative differences, long-term team structure, or even post-project follow-through, no unit is a legion, and these split opinions can easily shape not only the title itself, but the future of everyone who worked on it.

GTA 6 has mountains of references, including unique cosmetics! Let's take a look at how to find some plumber-worthy apparel.

Rockstar has faced public inquiries into the health of its developers over the monumental Grand Theft Auto 6, and union rumors have floated for weeks. With the vote finally coming through rejecting the recognition of said union, one staff member, named Thomas March, came out to explain why he thinks the team is better off without it, at least for now.

Discussion of the union representing Rockstar staff has been a rumor mill for weeks, with no clear answer about what's happening behind the scenes. Following an internal vote handled by a third party, Rockstar staff voted not to establish the IWGB as their union of choice, while maintaining the option to establish a union of their own at a later date.

In a post clarifying exactly what went down behind the scenes, Thomas March, an associate principal developer at Rockstar, described the IWGB’s position on Rockstar staff’s treatment as “endlessly frustrating…”. To March, the Independent Workers’ Union of Great Britain represented a bottleneck in staff voices, stopping individuals from arguing for their own benefits individually.

According to March, Rockstar’s worker treatment is nothing short of industry-leading. “Nowhere else have I been listened to so closely, treated with such respect, even while working with veterans and experts bar none.” Thomas claims that Rockstar’s treatment of each individual staff member means that formal recognition of a union isn’t really necessary.

When you’re making a big budget video game, it's likely different members of staff and development teams are going to clash.

Between flexible hours, employee benefits, and a truly caring workplace, March paints Rockstar as the fledgling developer’s dream, all the while decrying other staff members who raised complaints over crunch and questionable conditions of their own.

Rockstar staff does have its own internal union, dubbed the RSGWU, but the IWGB would have granted the staff unprecedented protections and argumentative power. While March cited the independence as a major boon, unions only get results when a staff force is unified. For now, they’ll have to make do with the RSGWU, a decent union that seems to have granted the team their own voice amongst investors.

The general response to March’s defense of the vote has been less than glowing, with dozens of fellow devs and union members decrying the result as short-sighted and selfish. Amidst the clapbacks and dismissals are former coworkers and industry peers lamenting a squandered chance, describing their own negative experiences with Rockstar’s internal face.

At the end of the day, each and every person can only share their individual experiences, each of which will paint their biases in a major deciding vote like Rockstar’s. The nature of the vote means that, should conditions fail to improve for everyone, members of Rockstar staff can try to recognize another union, or empower their current union to fight for their rights more actively.

Whether you believe Rockstar is a bastion of developer health or a corporate machine aiming for quality over all else, at current each individual member of Rockstar staff will need to choose.

Independent negotiations or small-scale union building is all they have at present, and while the recognition of the IWGB in such a prestigious studio could have made major waves, every individual is sure to vote for their own future.

#4225. A fat-burning molecule has an unexpected benefit for your muscles

Researchers have identified a naturally occurring molecule that plays a crucial role in building muscle strength and improving physical performance. Released during exercise, the molecule could also provide the basis for future treatments to protect against muscle damage associated with type 2 diabetes.

The molecule, known as L-β-aminoisobutyric acid (L-BAIBA), is essential for muscles to adapt to physical activity. It helps muscles become stronger, improves their resistance to fatigue, and protects against damage and weakness.

The study, published in Nature Communications and funded by Diabetes UK and the Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council (BBSRC), reveals that L-BAIBA is a central regulator of the biological changes that allow muscles to improve their strength, structure, and endurance in response to exercise training.

How Exercise Triggers a Natural Muscle Booster

Although the health benefits of exercise are well established, scientists still do not fully understand the biological processes that allow the body to adapt to physical demands. A research team led by Professor Lee Roberts at the University of Leeds investigated whether these processes could reveal new ways to treat chronic conditions such as type 2 diabetes.

L-BAIBA has attracted scientific interest for more than a decade. In research published in 2014, Roberts demonstrated that the molecule has beneficial effects on metabolism, helping to enhance the body's ability to burn fat in response to exercise. L-BAIBA is now commercially available as a dietary supplement.

The latest findings reveal another important function of the molecule. L-BAIBA acts as a chemical messenger that connects physical activity with beneficial changes in muscle structure and metabolism, helping muscles adapt to the demands placed on them.

Lee Roberts, Professor of Molecular Physiology and Metabolism at the University of Leeds, said: "Our research identifies L-BAIBA as an exercise-induced signal that helps muscles adapt, improve their metabolic capacity and ability to contract, and ultimately enhances physical performance.

"This gives us exciting new insight into how exercise benefits the body and highlights a promising target for future therapies aimed at preserving muscle function in chronic conditions such as diabetes."

Protecting Muscles Against Damage From Type 2 Diabetes

The researchers also discovered that L-BAIBA protects muscles against damage associated with type 2 diabetes. The condition can negatively affect muscle health, leading to a decline in muscle mass and strength, as well as disruptions in the way muscles process and use energy. These complications can significantly reduce a person's quality of life.

Because regular physical activity is an important part of managing type 2 diabetes, finding ways to improve muscle function and reduce fatigue could make a substantial difference for people who struggle to exercise.

Type 2 diabetes is a serious chronic condition that increases the risk of potentially life-threatening complications, including heart attacks and strokes. Its development is influenced by a complex combination of factors, including age, ethnicity, genetics, and living with overweight or obesity.

Although type 2 diabetes has traditionally been more common among older adults, diagnoses in people younger than 40 have been rising in recent years. Cases in this younger age group are now increasing more rapidly than among adults over 40.

A Promising Target for Future Diabetes Treatments

Anna Morris, Assistant Director of Research Strategy and Partnership at Diabetes UK, said: "Exercise plays an important role in managing type 2 diabetes, but for many people muscle weakness and fatigue can make staying active a real challenge. This research helps us better understand how muscles adapt to exercise and identifies a potential new target for improving muscle health. While these findings are still at an early stage, they could help shape future approaches that support people with type 2 diabetes to remain active and live healthier, longer lives."

Although the discovery opens promising avenues for future treatments, further research is needed to determine whether L-BAIBA supplementation can produce meaningful therapeutic benefits in people with type 2 diabetes.

The research was led by the University of Leeds in collaboration with:

The study was funded by Diabetes UK and BBSRC.

#4222. Harvard’s tiny UV light chip could help shrink quantum computers

Ultraviolet (UV) light is already essential to a wide range of modern technologies. Beyond its natural presence in sunlight, it is used to disinfect surfaces, make biological materials fluoresce, and manufacture computer chips through a process called photolithography. In the future, microscopic sources of UV light built directly into photonic chips could enable smaller quantum computers, ultra-precise atomic clocks, and other advanced technologies.

However, shrinking UV light sources to fit on a chip has presented a significant engineering challenge. Ultraviolet light rapidly loses power as it travels through optical waveguides, the tiny channels that carry light across a chip. This limitation has made it extremely difficult to develop compact UV sources with enough power for practical applications.

Now, a Harvard-led research team has demonstrated a microscopic photonic device that produces approximately 120 times more UV power than previous comparable devices. The researchers, working in the laboratory of Marko Lončar, the Tiantsai Lin Professor of Electrical Engineering, achieved the breakthrough using a widely studied material called thin-film lithium niobate.

Published in Nature Communications, the findings establish lithium niobate as a promising platform for generating powerful ultraviolet light in compact devices while minimizing optical losses.

Rather than trying to deliver ultraviolet light directly through microscopic channels, the researchers designed a device that generates UV light from red light within the chip itself.

The approach relies on a process known as frequency upconversion. Inside the lithium niobate crystal, two photons of red light combine to produce a single ultraviolet photon with higher energy. Lithium niobate is particularly well suited to this process because of its exceptional ability to convert light from one frequency to another.

"Our group is perhaps best known for utilizing lithium niobate for photonic devices that operate at longer, infrared wavelengths -- closer to the realm of telecommunications signals," Lončar said.

However, the team found that this transparent crystalline material, which has become increasingly important in integrated photonics, can also support light sources and guide light at much shorter wavelengths, including those in the ultraviolet range.

"When people think about [thin-film lithium niobate], they don't think of it as a UV material, but we show that it is," said co-first author Kees Franken, former research fellow in the Lončar lab. "We also show that there are some other nonlinear effects happening that we don't fully understand yet."

A New Technique Overcomes a Major Engineering Barrier

The device uses optical waveguides, microscopic channels etched into the lithium niobate film that direct light through the chip in much the same way electrical wires carry current.

For red light to be efficiently converted into ultraviolet light, the orientation of regions within the crystal must be repeatedly reversed at precisely controlled intervals along the waveguide. This manufacturing process, called poling, is a specialized technique used in nonlinear optics.

One of the biggest challenges has been creating these patterns with accuracy at scales smaller than a micrometer across devices that extend for centimeters.

Previous manufacturing methods required researchers to make an undesirable compromise. Poling the entire film before forming the waveguides made it difficult to correct manufacturing imperfections. Alternatively, creating the waveguides first reduced conversion efficiency because the electrodes were positioned too far away, allowing only part of the film to be successfully poled.

To eliminate this tradeoff, the Harvard team developed a technique they call "sidewall poling."

Precision Engineering Dramatically Improves Light Conversion

Instead of positioning the electrodes exclusively above the lithium niobate film, the researchers placed precisely patterned metal structures resembling tiny fingers directly alongside the etched waveguide. During fabrication, they applied a small voltage to permanently reverse the orientation of the crystal domains in a carefully controlled pattern.

"The key idea was: could we just put the electrodes directly on the waveguide?" said co-first author and former graduate student Soumya Ghosh. "It's a high-precision fabrication process to position the electrodes but requiring about 50-nanometer accuracy."

This arrangement enabled the researchers to reverse the crystal domains throughout the entire cross section of the waveguide, allowing light traveling through the material to undergo much more efficient frequency conversion.

The team could also fine-tune the spacing of the reversed crystal regions along the device. By incorporating existing "adapted poling" techniques previously developed in Lončar's laboratory and elsewhere, the researchers compensated for variations in the thickness of the lithium niobate film and the shape of the waveguide.

The resulting device generated 4.2 milliwatts of ultraviolet power directly on the chip at a wavelength of 390 nanometers. That represents approximately 120 times the output power achieved by the best previous thin-film lithium niobate devices operating in this wavelength range.

Earlier experiments using the material generated only tens of microwatts of UV power. Although those results demonstrated that the approach was scientifically feasible, the output was too low to support practical applications.

The substantial increase in power could be particularly valuable for trapped-ion quantum computers. These machines use electrically charged atoms to store and process quantum information. Many of the specific atomic energy transitions required to operate them involve light in the near-ultraviolet portion of the spectrum.

"If you want a scalable quantum computer that isn't the size of a truck, you need to scale everything down to the chip level, and this includes the light sources," Franken said.

The technology could also benefit ultra-precise atomic clocks and environmental monitoring systems. According to the researchers, the same range of ultraviolet wavelengths is well suited to compact sensors designed to closely monitor greenhouse gases and other atmospheric pollutants.

Franken and Ghosh attribute the breakthrough partly to the collaborative structure of Lončar's laboratory, where researchers carry out every stage of device development in one place, including theoretical research, engineering design, cleanroom fabrication, and optical testing.

"The hands-on intuition that we gained for how to make a device, while also keeping the zoomed-out view of what this device is for, and how we were going to characterize it -- that's a big part of what enabled this project for us," Ghosh said.

"Milliwatt-level UV generation using sidewall poled lithium niobate" was further co-authored by C.C. Rodrigues, J. Yang, C.J. Xin, S. Lu, D. Witt, G. Joe, G.S. Wiederhecker, and K.-J. Boller.

U.S. federal funding for the project came from the following sources: Department of the Air Force grant No. FA9453-23-C-A039; Office of Naval Research grant No. N00014-22-C-1041/VAS-21-0001; NASA grant No. 80NSSC22K0262 and 80NSSC23PB442; and National Science Foundation grants ERC EEC-1941583 and OMA-2137723.

Materials provided by Harvard John A. Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences. Original written by Anne J. Manning. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

#4220. 7 Details That Make GTA 6 A Flawed Game

Ronald is a video game journalist with more than 10 years of experience in the industry, working on several of the most important Spanish websites.

GTA 6 has become the highest-rated video game of all time according to Metacritic, sparking debate about whether it truly represents the closest thing to perfection in our history.

As someone who has enjoyed the series since the century's beginning, and who considers himself a huge fan of the Red Dead Redemption franchise, I have mixed feelings about this assertion, as the game's shortcomings are not hidden at any point.

Do these weaknesses diminish its revolutionary and utterly awe-inspiring nature? Not in the slightest, as it remains an extraordinary adventure that we will admire for decades, even with its imperfections.

Therefore, in order to discuss the game honestly and respectfully while also questioning the merits of its unparalleled achievements, here are seven details that make GTA 6 a flawed game.

Considering its draw distance, countless interactive elements, and dynamic entities that come alive in Leonida every second you walk, it's completely understandable that GTA 6 doesn't have a consistent frame rate.

Although this might say more about the platforms it was released on than the product itself, it certainly impacts the overall experience, especially in the most spectacular sequences where so many factors converge that the game seems on the verge of crashing.

As someone who grew up with such limited hardware that I had to play Hollow Knight at 15 FPS, I'd be lying if I said it was a negative aspect that bothered me too much, yet its easy and regularly noticeable nature is equally undeniable.

When the next-gen and PC versions arrive, I'm sure I'll have to update the article and remove this entry, but for now, it's the first drawback you notice, and it's impossible to ignore.

Striking the right pace for an open-world game's main story is among the most difficult tasks in the entire genre, as the chances of the player getting stuck, overwhelmed, or impatient are extremely high.

For better or worse, GTA 6 exposes itself to these pitfalls by presenting a campaign whose problem isn't necessarily its length, but rather the way many sections feel artificially stretched to reach such numbers.

The pacing is inconsistent, with entire hours of gameplay where the plot barely advances, only to have the entire storyline suddenly shift in specific moments, feeling like a vehicle accelerating and braking so hard it makes your back ache.

While Red Dead Redemption 2's story is roughly the same duration, Arthur Morgan's tale flows smoothly (let's forget about Guarma), and Jason and Lucia's, perhaps intentionally, suffer numerous ups and downs that disconnect you at times.

Grand Theft Auto 6 puts a large emphasis on keeping your relationship sound, so you need to know what ways are the best to raise the romance between Jason and Lucia.

Given GTA 6's size and complexity, the existence of bugs was entirely predictable, and it's rather surprising that, given the hardware, it doesn't include even more technical issues that hinder the player experience.

However, their presence occasionally transcends the anecdotal, with absurdly inconsistent autosaves that cause you to lose hours of progress, permanent weather conditions that don't change, NPCs that appear and disappear, and crashes that shut down the game without warning.

These are just what I've experienced firsthand, but reading anecdotes and watching footage shared online, it's clear that the plethora of errors is much greater, ranging from merely annoying to downright game-breaking.

It's light-years away from being like Cyberpunk 2077's launch, so the comparison is grossly unfair, but the fact that it's been a launch with irregularities is obvious and immediately apparent as soon as you start the game.

I admire the calm with which Rockstar chose to introduce us to the most anticipated video game in history, offering a prologue that, beyond mere formalities, actually extends to the end of Chapter 1.

The entire campaign, both narratively and in terms of gameplay, doesn't truly unfold until after 10 hours, during which you spend more time performing mundane tasks than interacting with GTA 6's rich systems.

Until then, the activities and objectives are quite limited, with few shootouts, no interactions with the police, minimal need for customization, and moderate interactions that only experience occasional bursts of intensity.

While I find this approach daring by AAA standards and think it's commendable, I believe that Colter in Red Dead Redemption 2 also has a slow start, yet with a far superior pace and impact, showing there's room for improvement.

As a result, since GTA 6 inherits its entire exoskeleton from Rockstar's latest release, I have no choice but to compare them directly, and it becomes clear which of the two does a better job of immersing the player in their first hours of gameplay.

This is a brief guide that entails the location of the Fast and Furious green Eclipse in GTA 6.

Since the studio hasn't lost its knack, understandable but erratic, for including dialogue in every commute, GTA 6 suffers from the same weakness that has plagued all the company's games for years.

I've lost count of how many times conversations between characters are interrupted because, since they're tied to the distance between two points, it's common to arrive quickly at your destination only to have the exchange end prematurely.

I know they introduced the option to read the conversation history from the pause menu, but for Rockstar to offer this as their solution to such a long-standing and annoying problem seems truly poor.

It might sound nitpicky, though it breaks the immersion and makes you miss parts of the plot and the relationships between characters, so it's not appropriate to underestimate the issue's magnitude.

Speaking of perpetuating past transgressions, it's surprising how the morality system is an idea replicated ad nauseam in the video game industry, yet virtually no one can implement it successfully.

In this case, you again have a spectrum that oscillates between being a saint or a devil based on specific actions that feel terribly gamified rather than immersive, as they're more of a checklist of behaviors and actions than a genuine human scale.

That petting a cat has a positive impact, just as robbing a drug caravan by only shooting dozens of thugs in the knees is an interesting way to approach the ethical behavior of our protagonists, who will still canonically steal and murder no matter how hard you try to be good.

It's an arbitrary and artificial metric, and while it's partially redeemed by being a measure of criminal professionalism rather than civic morality, it's difficult to reconcile such a realistic and captivating world with a system of emojis that determine your worth as a criminal.

Even just having the system work behind the scenes in accordance with our natural inclinations, like Dishonored, without forcing any kind of action but allowing us to discover the consequences of our moves organically, would be much better, so it feels like a missed opportunity.

Some players may think they should register a hot new sports car as their starter car. There's actually a better choice. Here's the best starter car to register in GTA VI.

Video games find in technology the key to their existence, as it's the mechanism that allows interaction and, therefore, gives meaning to these magical digital worlds in which we can completely blend ourselves.

Consequently, the fact that GTA 6 is the most impressive technical feat we've seen in the industry is enough to consider it revolutionary, yet it deeply troubles me that this capability is used to enhance realism rather than gameplay.

When I'm allowed to perform an action in a title that only tells me how incredibly well-programmed it is, instead of said action serving a purpose within the thematic and gameplay loop its title proposes, it's just empty boasting.

Exercising, grocery shopping, refueling, or eating food are impressive in how they're animated and integrated, though none of them truly contribute to the overall gameplay experience that GTA aims to offer; they could disappear, and it would be completely unnoticeable.

Certainly, there's no such thing as necessary or unnecessary in art, so realism for its own sake also has its place. Regardless, I can't help but think that it slows everything down, and as the hours pass, it distracts you, even if only for a few seconds, from the truly captivating things hidden within the state of Leonida.

Like many games, Grand Theft Auto 6 is full of easter eggs for you to discover. These are some of the best Leonida has to offer.

#4219. Exclusive – Behind The Romance: Rockstar Talks GTAVI’s Jason And Lucia

After dozens of hours exploring Leonida, I have a lot of positive things to say about Grand Theft Auto VI, and shared as much in our review of the game. But for my part, the feature that elevated the game most prominently above Rockstar Games’ other (excellent) games wasn’t its graphics, missions, or action – it was the storytelling and interplay between the two lead protagonists. Jason and Lucia bring heart, emotional depth, and a sense of genuine threat to the crime fantasy, as you grow attached to them and start cheering for them against all the odds stacked against them.

We reached out to senior members of the Rockstar Games team to ask about their thoughts on Jason and Lucia, and this is what they had to share.

During my playthrough, the Jason and Lucia dynamic really elevated the experience, adding heart and emotional weight to the expected mix of action, driving, and activities around Leonida. Was a couple or romantic relationship the plan or goal for the game from very early on in development, or did that come later? Do you see the focus on Jason and Lucia’s relationship as one of the features that separates Grand Theft Auto VI from your prior work on storytelling in the game series?

Stephen Donkin, Vice President of Design: “The dual protagonists and the relationship between the two of them was there from very early in development, but exactly how that was expressed in the game did change over time. It was an enormous challenge for us to get them working together in the open world together and finding exactly how that would work. As we started to layer in more mechanics, dialogue, and incremental features across all teams, it just clicked at some point. The ability to be together in the open world also allowed us for new ways to tell the story of the game and to bring some of the exposition and narrative into the open world in a way we hadn’t been able to do before. Hearing these little bits of dialogue as you are just tooling around the world that have specific context to what you as a player have just been doing in the story really knits it all together.”

The player has a choice for how to develop the relationship between the two leads, but I imagine most players are drawn toward helping it thrive. In early playtests, is that what you observed?

Katie Pica, Design Director: Player Systems & Progression:“Overall, we’ve seen that players are invested in supporting Jason and Lucia’s relationship but we don’t favor a specific path through the game, it is completely down to player choice.”

It feels like a lot of the game’s driving narrative beats factor for a close connection between Jason and Lucia. Was it challenging to craft variations that included a more tense or distant connection between the two? Is that even possible?

Luke Howard, Senior Design Director: Missions & Visualization:“One of the core goals of this game was to tell the story of Jason and Lucia with a base line relationship where they are amicable, if just platonic, as they still share the same ultimate goals and need each other to achieve them. So, this gave us a good platform on the main flow to expand particularly intense or emotional moments they experience with variation that can expand on their romantic relationship, while not losing anything if that doesn’t exist. In short, we did develop variation in scenes and interactions that range from subtle to more significant, but done in a way that should feel authentic to the player’s choices, relationship-wise and also criminal profile.

One example is after Lucia helps Kordell’s gang pull off an intense armored truck robbery she shares the information with Raul’s crew. Afterwards Jason pulls Lucia aside to see how she's coping. This moment carries several variations where the performance direction was captured multiple ways to cover a range emotional energy between them. The actors deliveries are brilliant and nuanced – these small tender moments are where we tried to craft pieces that when added up together over the course of the story, author an authentic version of the player’s Jason and Lucia.”

Were there any fictional couples or real-life couples that the team looked at for inspiration in shaping the Jason and Lucia dynamic, whether those couples came from big crime stories or not?

Rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“We definitely started by looking at all the “couple on the run” movies. There are a lot of them but the ones that we kept coming back to were Warren Beatty and Faye Dunaway in Bonnie and Clyde, McQueen and MacGraw in The Getaway (the Jim Thomson book is also great), True Romance, Thelma and Louise. Clooney and JLo’s dynamic in Out of Sight, as well. And then a lot of buddy movies actually – Riggs and Murtaugh, Butch and Sundance, Mike Lowry and Marcus Burnett, etc. for their back and forth together. In terms of having a game where the characters can change based on how you play and whether you really lean into and enjoy the crime spree we thought about how both Pulp Fiction and Natural Born Killers start with a couple in a diner pulling out guns, but then how different those couples are and how different those scenarios play out. Jason and Lucia are a lot tougher than Tim Roth and Amanda Plummer but we liked the idea of telling a story where Jason and Lucia could end up being closer to either end of that spectrum based on what the player was doing.”

Sex and intimacy are notoriously complicated and challenging to present in games. How did you aim to strike a balance with their private moments together that felt authentic? Any thoughts about how or why it’s so challenging to present adult relationships in video games?

Rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“This is definitely something we thought a lot about and spent a long time trying to get right. The actors who play Jason and Lucia were so good, and they had a natural chemistry and part of it was just trying to capture some of that.

There’s this trade off in making games between player control and then scripted scenarios. We try and give the player as much control as we can because we are working in an interactive medium and actually doing something rather than watching it is going to feel more powerful. But then you have the ability to really mess around and break the illusion of a tender or romantic moment or whatever it is. So the relationship aspect of this story is there if a player wants to engage in it, but if they don’t the story can play out differently.”

In its best moments of genuine support, regular connection, open communication, and flirty or engagement with one another, Jason and Lucia can come across as a pretty ideal model of good relationships – even while they’re simultaneously committing major crimes together. Was that juxtaposition of a healthy romantic relationship against an external world of illicit activity an explicit goal for how the narrative came together?

Rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“That was the goal, yes. You are really living with these characters – they’re eating, sleeping, showering, throwing away their trash, or not. The relationship needed to feel real to sit alongside all of that. Then even just as a development team, we live with these characters for years and years. We wanted them to be people we could like, care about, and root for. And they needed to like each other. But then the world itself is so crazy and chaotic and seemingly on the brink of collapse.

When we set out to make this game, and go into that multiyear development marathon, we said we wanted to spend our time working on something with heart, and with some characters you could care about and root for. It’s barely worth even stating, but we are living in a time when people are divided along almost every line, and feelings about the future are pretty bleak. We wanted to create a world that held up a mirror to that, showed that fever pitch of craziness that we are all maybe a couple of bad decisions away from, but we wanted the story we were going to tell to have something positive at its core and the message that human connection is better than division.”

The game automatically moves you to play one character or another at certain points, but for many sequences, you can choose your playable lead. In your experience playing and watching others play, do most players gravitate toward one character or another as “their character?”

Stephen Donkin, Vice President of Design:“It really varied in our playthroughs. They are both such great characters and performances that people seemed to gravitate to both of them in different ways. But overall, we have found the split of time between characters to be relatively even on a per-playthrough and also at a macro level.”

Revenant XSpark played the Predator League with Lightningfast, hellff, Hoax, deecee and Venka. Rinsat, now listed on Revenant XSpark’s roster alongside Hoax, Techno, venka, k1ngkappa and Madelyn, appeared in Kryon’s lineup for that event.

Riot Games and JioBLAST are running the playoffs online as an eight-team double-elimination bracket from 23 to 29 November. The South Asian qualifiers will be joined at the Last Chance Qualifier by one team from Oceania and the runner-up of the SEA Kickoff Playoffs. ONE Up is organising that event with Riot Games.

#4216. Why Do I Want To Paint The Walls In Grand Theft Auto VI?

I admire the cozy sim genre. Stardew Valley and Animal Crossing are on regular rotation in my home on my family’s screens, but not my own. In an odd way, I find the genre stressful, arguably the opposite of its intended purpose. I will happily and cathartically guide Grace Ashcroft through the tense hallways of Rhodes Hill in Resident Evil Requiem, but Pokémon Pokopia’s seemingly endless list of to-dos makes me sweat. It’s just not my genre, and I have come to terms with that.

Grand Theft Auto VI is not a cozy game, but it has a substantial amount of cozy elements and mechanics. Bird (and animal) watching, for example, is apparent and encouraged early in the experience. You can also fix up your somewhat dilapidated home from almost the moment you are let loose outside of the opening tutorial missions.

And for some reason, I couldn’t start that process fast enough.

I climbed to the roof to fix the leak and replaced all the stairs leading up to the home before I ever participated in the game’s namesake and stole a car. Normally, it’s the kind of interaction I skip or choose not to engage with, given the option. Or, I do the bare minimum to progress. Sure, I have all the options in the world to build and decorate a house and make it my own, but… that feels like a lot of work. And I am not an artist.

The “cozy” elements of Grand Theft Auto VI are admittedly different from those in a game like Pokopia or Animal Crossing. You’re not designing your home (though you can pick a paint color), but it feels similar, and I am trying to figure out why I enjoy it here as opposed to other games. Is it because Jason and Lucia are so instantly believable as human beings that I want their home to be nicer?

After some thought, I think it might just come down to Grand Theft Auto VI’s consistently impressive visual fidelity. Replacing the shingles on the roof, for example, offers a close-up look at Jason’s character model, and you can practically feel the texture of the asphalt while the heat of the sun beats down.

I don’t have confirmation, but it also just feels like someone at Rockstar did exhaustive research on what the process of replacing a roof shingle should look like, even if, I’m sure, it probably doesn’t quite work that way in the real world. Jason makes it look incredibly easy, to the point that it had me questioning if I should be climbing up to my own roof and taking care of some loose shingles myself. And you know what is a lot of fun? Watching someone who is good at something do the thing they’re good at.

I’m now into the driving and shooting part of the game (and enjoying that, too!), but I am shocked at how grateful I was to have the option to stay home and put up drywall.

The day Arc Raiders launched, it peaked at 264,673 concurrent players on Steam. Although not massive, it was quite a bit more than the game’s most popular - free - beta test managed to attract.

According to SteamDB, the game peaked at 462,488 concurrent players on Steam, which is a sizeable increase on its launch day numbers. Indeed, should this trend continue, Arc Raiders is going to be well on its way to doubling its initial launch record.

While a few games have broken their launch Steam player records in the past, it’s incredibly rare to see it happen - especially twice in such a short period after launch. Embark clearly has a winner on its hands here.

Arc Raiders’ next big moment is the game’s first post-launch map, which is set to arrive at some point this month, alongside new Quests and other gameplay items. Today's Battlefield 6 patch is laser-focused on taking care of some of the more infuriating bugs while also taking out a couple of exploits.

The next Battlefield 6 update is here. Having gone live just moments ago, update 1.1.1.5 is something of a midseason update, bringing a few quality of life tweaks to the game alongside some key fixes for a few of the issues that cropped up since the launch of Season 1 in late October.

This latest release is also the first to tackle some of the problems players have been running into playing Redsec battle royale, the free-to-play component that also came out recently.

Another exploit the patch fixes is the one that allowed players to stand on the Recon Drone and reach areas they’re not supposed to. This was done by… repeatedly hitting it with a Sledgehammer. In terms of battle royale, the patch has a few fixes that should help make the experience more consistent, as well as improve the flow of matches. One of the more interesting addresses an issue that could eliminate the entire squad instead of reviving dead teammates when using a Mobile Spawn.

Patch 1.1.1.5 also has yet more adjustments to weapon dispersion (bloom). Some of the casses it addresses include transitioning from sprint to firing in ADS, and others where it apparently scaled with player movement speed.

#4211. GTA 6: Complete Beginner's Guide

Usama Mehmood is a Senior Writer at DualShockers with more than five years of experience in the video game industry. He has been writing professionally since 2021 and covering games since 2022, with work spanning guides, lists, reviews, and features across action-adventure games, JRPGs, open-world titles, racing games,

Pretty sure we’ve all had an eventful week with Grand Theft Auto 6 so far because it is undoubtedly the most ambitious video game release, shattering an entertainment-product record on release and going way beyond people’s expectations with the amount of detail and what it has in store. And undeniably, anyone jumping in for the first time may feel overwhelmed by the mechanics and additions.

Grand Theft Auto 6 delivers an enormous open world, a gripping story, a vibrant Vice City and an astonishing range of activities.

But hey, whether you’re a seasoned veteran of the series or totally new to video games who’s playing this blindly for the first time, you don’t have to worry because I've put together an extensive Beginner’s Guide to GTA 6 that compiles the most helpful tips and explanations of the game’s most complex aspects. Strap in, because this will be worth your time, trust.

I’m getting the formalities out of the way first because I’m quickly going to suggest tuning some settings right from the main menu or even in-game, actually. These are all up to you, but I’m mostly here to show you how each one can be helpful.

First, if you’re used to the OG controls of the GTA series, quickly set the control scheme to Classic, as this brings back some familiar GTA 5-style inputs. By default, running and sprinting are mapped to clicking L3, while jumping is assigned to X (A on Xbox). Switching to Classic moves running and sprinting back to X (A), puts crouching on L3, and swaps a few other actions around. I genuinely find it much more comfortable, especially if you've spent years playing the older games.

Next, I'd recommend setting your Minimap to Always On under UI > Navigation. GTA 6's default Dynamic HUD can hide certain information when you're exploring, which looks great for immersion but isn't always practical when you're still learning your way around Leonida. And while you’re at it, reduce Motion Blur Strength if you don’t want to get sick.

And beyond whichever aiming sensitivity suits you, be sure to experiment with the Targeting settings under Gameplay > Combat. Partial is a good middle ground for newcomers, as it helps move your aim towards nearby targets without completely locking onto them. Finally, in UI > Units of Measurement, you can choose your preferred unit system, like the 12-hour clock over the 24-hour one.

Grand Theft Auto 6 puts a large emphasis on keeping your relationship sound, so you need to know what ways are the best to raise the romance between Jason and Lucia.

Briefly going over this as well, since you can easily handle this, contrary to what other players might have you believe. Jason and Lucia are your own, like the little make-believe babies for a class project. Besides their relationship, keep in mind that these characters now have individual stats, like hunger, muscle mass, weight, and sleep management. These can actively influence gameplay in a few ways, such as sleep affecting your total stamina. Meanwhile, things like weight affect how fast you can sprint.

We already have a list of the best ways to boost the couple’s relationship, but the basic gist that you need to remember is not to let them drop to Partners in Crime or below. There are plenty of things that can help you easily boost their relationship, so it’s honestly impossible to not maintain it unless you’re purposely not using both characters or sabotaging it yourself.

And since we’re here, make sure to actively invest in the couple’s BuckMe Family Savings account later on until you max it out at the highest tier, since both that and their relationship are among the primary factors influencing the ending of GTA 6.

Again, you’re free to check our dedicated guide on the mechanic as well, but with the Criminal Profile system, just think of it as a more approachable karma system, like the Honor one from Red Dead 2. This is also one of the other parameters that can influence GTA 6’s ending. A lot of people will have you believe that it strips away your maniacal “GTA” playstyle, but trust me, with everything in your power, this is the most forgiving and manipulable mechanic in the game.

The only thing to watch out for is taking things to the “Irredeemable” state because by that point you can’t revert it back, and you’ll be stuck with that profile unless you have a save file. You can achieve and maintain a Professional Criminal Profile by simply being a good citizen or trying to have as few casualties as possible during side activities, or even successfully making clean getaways and stealth takedowns.

Don’t be afraid to take headshots when necessary because even if you reach a state like Psycho, you can easily change that back by petting a couple of domestic animals, spending some casual time with each other, or just by avoiding headshots altogether for the next few kills by shooting in the limbs instead.

GTA 6 has a noticeably more complex Wanted System than its predecessors. For starters, we’re back to six Wanted Stars, and the police are now much more observant of our actions. Witnesses can report your crimes, security cameras can capture your current identity, and even certain high-end vehicles have trackers that forbid you from just stealing them. In other words, no more crazy Grand Theft Auto-ing.

The biggest change, however, is the introduction of the Heat system. Even after you've managed to lose the cops, they will still remember certain identifying details about you, including your appearance, clothing, getaway vehicle, visible weapons, and whether Jason and Lucia were together. These are represented by small red icons underneath your Wanted Stars, so pay attention to them whenever you're trying to escape.

It’s either how fast you can clear the heat markers off of you in the natural way or some creative tactics that I can suggest, like using water vehicles or boats for escaping higher-level wanted stars, since the rivers and sea tend to be open and less swamped with traffic than VC’s urban infrastructure.

Money plays a much bigger role in GTA 6 than you might initially expect, and you'll quickly find yourself needing extra cash to purchase weapons, clothing for both characters, vehicle upgrades, and other necessities. Thankfully, Leonida is practically overflowing with opportunities to make a quick buck. But the progression works steadily throughout each chapter here.

You’ll start off small by robbing convenience stores and other local businesses in chapter 2, but by chapters 3 and 4, the Robberies tab on your map will be almost flooded with bigger opportunities, including pawn shops, jewelry stores, and banks. Even the occasional gang hideout has different valuables like unique guns to own, vehicles to sell, or safes to bust open and loot.

However, be mindful that robbing a place blind isn't always the smartest idea since many of these sites have security cameras and alarms. Try to use Focus Mode as much as possible to identify enemies, valuable items, and locate safe combinations before making your escape.

Of course, not everything in Leonida requires you to point a gun at someone. There are several side activities that can help you earn some extra money, including stealing vehicles for buyers like Moses and Randy, hunting wildlife for Bret, and competing in Demolition Derbies at Ambrosia Raceway.

One final thing worth remembering is that GTA 6 has three forms of allowance: pocket cash, bank savings, and the valuables you carry in your stash bag. While your bank balance is safe, getting Wasted or Busted can cost you the cash you're carrying, along with any stolen goods you haven't managed to sell, so make a habit of visiting ATMs to deposit your earnings into BuckMe whenever possible.

Many of us are already feeling nostalgic about GTA 6’s first chapter; I mean, seriously, the vibe in Key Lento is unparalleled, especially when playing the game for the first time. But as all things come and go, the vibe doesn't last for long here.

There are a handful of missables you can easily overlook if you rush through the story, so I'd strongly recommend taking your time and exploring everything the Keys have to offer before moving on. Without spoiling, The Tourist Trap mission marks the point of no return for Chapter 1's free roam, so make sure you’re fully ready.

For starters, make sure you complete Shirley's optional jobs, Get Shirley's Rum and Steal the Scooter, as these are exclusive to the first chapter. You might also want to check the loose floorboards for any money you've stashed away, and deposit that into your BuckMe Family Savings.

Lastly, it doesn’t hurt to have a separate manual save for this chapter specifically since GTA 6 doesn't currently let you replay completed story missions, so having a backup gives you the opportunity to revisit Key Lento without having to start another playthrough.

You don't necessarily need to complete every single activity before moving on, but I'd hate for you to miss out on some of the more interesting encounters and neat discoveries Rockstar’s tucked away in this opening chapter. Trust me, you'll appreciate this thing the most here.

Grand Theft Auto 6 makes you lose everything at the end of the first chapter, so make sure that you complete these necessary tasks before taking the plunge into chapter two.

#4210. Grand Theft Auto VI's Auto Drive Is A Beautiful And Free Version Of Hands-Free Travel

Grand Theft Auto VI is a game where you spend a lot of time behind the wheel. Always has been. But sometimes, you just won't feel like actively driving, but you also don't to waste money on a cab.

This is where Auto Drive comes in. It lets the game take over and drive you where you need to go in real time and all with a cinematic camera that shifts and moves, letting you take in the environment without all that pesky "having to pay attention to the road." Red Dead Redemption 2 had the same feature, and I have fond memories of taking advantage of it to watch Arthur ride his horse through that game's incredible environment. It's a great option in GTAVI, but how to use it and turn it on isn't immediately apparent.

First, you must select a destination. Get the GPS set up to direct you to where you want to go.

Next, start driving. The Auto Drive is smart, but doesn't seem to be smart enough to make three-point turns or back out of parking lots. You need to be on your way before you can turn it on.

Once you're on the path, hold down in the d-pad and press start to activate Cinematic.

Once you've done this you should be able to hold down the Circle button on PlayStation or the B button on Xbox to activate Auto Drive and... voilà! You can sit back and let Jason or Lucia take the wheel. They will drive legally, even stopping at lights, but you can speed them up if they're taking too long.

I've always enjoyed driving in Grand Theft Auto, but I was grateful to find this almost-hidden option early in the game.

#4209. Arc Raiders has proven that extraction shooters can be popular, with over 4 million copies sold in under two weeks

Arc Raiders has sold even more copies, which we should've guessed, given that the game keeps breaking its own concurrent player records.

It’s pretty clear at this stage that Arc Raiders is one of the biggest launches of 2025. More interesting than the numbers themselves, however, is that this is an extraction shooter - a subgenre which has typically been thought of as niche.

If you’ve been paying the PvPvE game any attention, you could easily see how (and why) it keeps breaking its own records.

Today, publisher Nexon announced in a press release (via Gematsu) that Arc Raiders has now sold over 4 million copies. The game came out on October 30, which means it managed to sell that many copies in a little over 10 days.

The news comes on the same day that developer Embark Studios announced that the game had more than 700,000 concurrent players across all platforms over the weekend. Over the same weekend on Steam alone, Arc Raiders broke its own Steam concurrent record with a new peak of 462,488 players - which is a significant chunk of that 700,000+ player base.

This marks the second time the extraction shooter has broken its own concurrent player records, which is something very few games have managed in the past. Arc Raiders remains a top-seller, too. On Steam, it’s currently the second-best seller globally (by revenue), sitting just below Counter-Strike 2.

“The many different ways you play and participate in ARC Raiders have completely blown us away, going far beyond what we ever imagined. You surprise us, you outsmart us, and you keep us on our toes. We wouldn’t have it any other way,” the developer wrote on Twitter.

Embark recently published a roadmap to highlight all the new content coming to the game over the remainder of this year. The first new map is set to arrive this month alongside new Arc units, new gameplay items, new events and more.

If you’re currently hooked on this gem of a game, we guarantee that our Arc Raiders gameplay tips will have at least one you didn’t know about. We also have more guides on how to find some of the more elusive items in the game, such as olives, lemons and apricots, and prickly pears.

#4208. Blackwater Mill is an ambitious, if flawed, horror game from a small Yorkshire studio

It seems as though every facet of American society has been explored in horror, from the high towers of luxury to the dark backwoods. But the same is not true of other countries, including the UK, especially with so many dark, decrepit corners to explore. That's what Yorkshire bashed Wrenhaven Ltd. are looking to resolve with their upcoming mobile horror game Blackwater Mill.

Blackwater Mill sees you step into the role of Sam, the project manager for the demolition of the titular mill. Venturing up into the Pennine mountains of Yorkshire during a dark, rainy night, you find yourself trapped in the mill, and it's up to you to find out what happened to leave it infested with the unquiet dead.

Miller lite Now let's address the elephant in the room, or the mine at least. Blackwater Mill is not a particularly good-looking game; in fact, you might say it looks positively crude. But, equally, I can't help but admire the ambition Wrenhaven Ltd. has put into this. A five-chapter horror game is ambitious even for full studios, let alone a tiny indie.

And, in truth, there's not much in the way of Brit horror on other platforms, let alone on mobile. If you've never had the pleasure of visiting abandoned mines on a tour, and feeling the all-pervading darkness when the lights go out, it's hard to describe how mesmerising and terrifying it can be.

To be honest, if you can get past the initial (very) janky graphics, there's something also rather unnerving about Blackwater Mill's undead miners. And while it may not sway those of you who want a high-fidelity experience on mobile, it's well worth a look when it does release for Android very soon, and iOS later.

In the meantime, if you want to see what other spine-chillers there are on mobile, why not take a look at our list of the best horror games on Android? Featuring plenty of bona fide terrors to keep you up these long winter nights.

Fnatic have signed Czech duelist Martin 'marteen' Pátek from Gentle Mates as their first new player for VCT EMEA 2027. The London club are rebuilding after missing Champions for the first time in the team's history.

The London club’s new duelist is a player who hurt them badly in 2026. Colin ‘CoJo’ Johnson is listed as manager of the rebuilt roster.

The move still has one step left. Pley.gg listed the signing as still awaiting approval from Riot Games. The link is not new. Word of a verbal agreement between marteen and Fnatic emerged on 24 September. That was about a month before Gentle Mates released their whole roster.

Marteen still finished VCT EMEA Stage 2 as the team’s top-rated player, with a rating of 1.23. The signing follows a clear-out of long-serving players. Boaster had been with Fnatic since 3 February 2021. Alfajer arrived on 9 May 2022, and crashies on 11 December 2024.

Marteen’s own spell at Gentle Mates ran from 20 November 2025 to 25 October 2026. The two rosters are now tied together by the same transfer window.

Gentle Mates had already cleared their own decks. All five players on the active roster and both coaches were let go before the club’s first season as a VCT partner team.

For a British organisation, the swap leaves Fnatic’s identity in new hands. Boaster had been the longest-serving name in the departing group. Kaajak and Cloud are now the continuity, with marteen as the headline addition.

#4206. Arc Raiders' new map will be unlocked through a community event that starts today, and everyone has to donate

It looks like it's going to take the Arc Raiders community a bit of work to unlock the game's next map.

As many of Arc Raiders’ regular players predicted, the game’s first post-launch map won’t just be available for everyone, it will instead be closely tied to a community event. Breaking New Ground is the name of that event, and it’s one where everyone will need to contribute in order to rebuild some old tunnels and unlock the way to Stella Montis.

The event kicks off today alongside the release of the game’s latest patch. The ask is relatively simple: players must commit Basic Materials to the project so that the tunnels can be rebuilt. This option will be available to anyone who’s played at least five rounds.

If you’ve spent any time in Arc Raiders, you’ll know that Basic Materials are things like Metal parts, Fabric, Chemicals, Rubber Parts, and Plastic Parts - most of which are easy to find in the game’s various maps.

Even beyond the ultimate goal of unlocking the new map, donations will also reward you with Merits, which is a new event currency, though there’s a cap on how many you can earn.

Once enough materials have been collected, the next phase of the event, Staking Our Claim, will begin, which will bring a new progression track to the game, and make Stella Montis available for players to visit.

Developer Embark describes the new environment as unlike any that we have seen in the game so far. It’s a facility carved into the northern mountains, which means it’s going to have a near-pristine look; quite the contrast with the rest of the game’s environments.

Stella Montis also has its own Arc enemies, loot, schematics, and other gameplay items. You can look forward to coming across the Shredder, a close-quarter Arc unit exclusive to the new map for now.

Then there’s The Matriarch, a somehow even larger version of the Queen. Thankfully, it will only be available under a specific map condition, so you’re in no danger of running into her randomly. The update will also introduce a new legendary weapon, two new grenades, and three new mines.

Staking Our Claim will only run until December, which is when the next stage of the game’s roadmap will kick off. Then, the Cold Snap update will introduce the Flickering Flames event, the first snowfall Map Condition, and the Expedition Project voluntary wipe.

In case you’re still missing them, here’s how to find lemons and apricots, prickly pear, and olives.

#4204. Zenless Zone Zero's new Krampus squad know when you've been bad or good in a Christmas-y update to close out 2025

Zenless Zone Zero's 2.4 update is a chunky one, adding a new faction to the action RPG's roster alongside a new area, and fresh playable characters.

Zenless Zone Zero’s latest Special Program was a big one, bringing us all the news about Version 2.4, the next major update. It’s called On the Precipice of the Abyss, and it will be available to download on November 26.

On the Precipice of the Abyss has tendrils in many areas of the game, touching several parts of its fiction as well as gameplay, so it’s one to watch out for.

Version 2.4’s biggest claim to fame is the introduction of the Krampus Compliance Authority, a new faction that’s affiliated with TOPS. This looks to be the oversight committee, dispatched after the squad’s adventure beneath Timesworn Hill.

The events of this narrative arch follow on from the Timesworn Hill crisis, which is partly why we’re going to a new area as part of this update. The old mining site can now be explored for the first time in a decade, now that the Miasma has begun to recede.

Our newcomers this time around are Dialyn and Banyue. Dialyn is an S-Rank Physical Stun Agent who’s a former customer service specialist. This isn’t just a backstory, however, as it plays into her gameplay.

Dialyn relies on two resources: Customer Complaint and Positive Review, but her core role is to stun enemies and allow teammates to unleash their Ults, with a nice boost to boot.

Banyue is another S-Rank, though he’s a Fire Rupture Agent. He uses his martial arts expertise to create combinations of might and grandeur. In combat, he pulls from Adrenaline and Wrathful Fires, alternating between the two to fuel his actions. There’s a bit of rhythm to his gameplay that might take you a little while to master.

Even more characters will join as part of this update, in the form of not one but two new Bangboo units. Birkblick is Krampus' own proprietary lil bunny fella, who brings a sensor array that can transform into a cannon in combat, essentially tracking and immediately nuking targets. Then there’s Bild N. Boolok, a Support Agent-affiliated Physical damage dealing Bangboo bringing a giant block hammer to the fight to, well, smash enemies with.

It’s a bit of a winter party in Version 2.4, it seems, as the update will bring back Hugo (Attack - Ice), and Ellen (Attack - Ice), too.

You can also look forward to the return of the Bangboo auto chess event, which now includes PvE stages with unique rewards. In fact, playing this event is how you could get Bild N. Boolok for free. Lightstream Notes is another event that will be available for the duration of this update, and it will let you tag along with Ye Shunguang to New Eridu.

#4203. Knight & Dragon Side Story turns the text-based JRPG from turn-based to real-time

We cover a lot of smaller, more niche series on the site here. And one of them that has recently cropped up is Knight & Dragon, a text-based JRPG series full of plenty of number-crunching and grind. Now, developer Shinjiro Nakagawa is trying something new with the launch of Knight & Dragon Side Story.

As you may have already gleaned from the headline, the core change of Knight & Dragon Side Story is that it ditches the traditional turn-based JRPG combat in favour of real-time action. It's not fully 3D, however, as instead you'll be tasked with actively dodging attacks in the style of something like Undertale, making for a more fast-paced adventure.

For me, the only issue is the traces of AI art seen in some of the icons, at least to my eye. Which is a shame because I think part of the charm of the Knight & Dragon series is the way in which they work by using text and basic icons. You lose some of that with the generated assets.

Still, if you're willing to give it a shot, I reckon that this will present a very interesting departure from the norm for fans of Knight & Dragon. And you can find it right now on iOS and Android!

In the meantime, though, if you want, you can find some of the other big releases on mobile that we think are worth playing in one simple place. Our list of the five new mobile games to try this week offers some interesting picks which we think are worth checking out.

#4202. Battlefield 6 gets a new map today alongside major changes to controller aim assist, and even more weapon dispersion tweaks

Right on schedule, the latest Battlefield 6 patch has arrived to kick off the next stage of Season 1.

Battlefield 6’s first season has entered its second phase. The game received a major update earlier today, version 1.1.2.0, which delivers a host of changes to the game, many of which have been expected.

The update, of course, also adds new content to the game in the form of the map Eastwood, as well as new hardware and fresh features for the multiplayer sandbox.

We’ve known about the new content side of today’s patch for quite some time. The update kicks off the California Resistance stage of Season 1, which is the second of three. The new Eastwood map takes place in California, and it’s a map cut from the larger Battlefield Redsec battle royale map of Fort Lyndon.

There’s a new limited-time mode called Sabotage - a tactical, 8v8 mode where two teams attempt to destroy as many bomb sites as possible. The other big new feature that arrives today is Battle Pickups.

These are powerful weapons which can be found in specific game modes (and in Portal), scattered around the map for players to pick up and use. They have limited ammo that cannot be replenished, and deliver incredible firepower.

Redsec players have a new Gauntlet mission to look forward to that joins the existing modes. It’s called Rodeo and it involves a lot of vehicular action. Finally, everyone gets to unlock two new weapons: the the DB-12 shotgun, and the M327 Trait revolver sidearm. There’s also a new angled grip attachment.

The fixes and tweaks side of the patch is arguably the more interesting. Controller aim assist has received a big overhaul that essentially resets everything to open beta settings. The goal is to make infantry targeting more consistent.

Controller players actually get the bulk of the changes in this update, which also improves input latency and stick response. Several issues that reset aim assist values, or make it behave erratically, have been addressed.

The conversation around weapon bloom/spread doesn’t look like it’s ever going to end, because Battlefield Studios is yet again tuning gunplay to fix unintended dispersion behaviour, and decrease its intensity across the board.

Certain Challenges have had their description rewritten so their requirements can be better understood. Beyond that, you can expect several deployables to behave much more consistently, including several bug fixes there, too.

Head to the official blog for the full rundown of patch 1.1.2.0.
