AI: The Somnium Files – nirvanA Initiative is one of the most interesting visual novels we’ve played through in a while. The murder mystery at its heart is brought to life by some great writing and quirky characters alongside the satisfyingly integrated, beautifully balanced Psync puzzle elements.

Even with some minor control issues, there is a lot to love in this game, even if you never picked up the original. Highly recommended if you're even a little bit curious.

The Nintendo eShop would be a considerably more exciting and interesting place if it were packed full of games like Ape Out. It’s a refreshingly original experience that more than deserves a place in any Switch owner’s library.

Difficult, frenetic gameplay, strong art direction, and an even stronger jazz drum soundtrack make this the sort of memorable game that you’ll likely keep coming back to over and over for another few runs in arcade mode. Ape Out gets a strong recommendation to anyone looking for a distinct and unforgettable game for their Switch collection; it’s a bit of an acquired taste, but well worth your time.

BALL x PIT is a tremendous brew of so many ideas it ought to collapse under the confusion. However, it operates in such perfect balance that it appeals both to the one-more-go instinct and to more cerebral planning and creativity. Kenny Sun Studios set itself a heck of a challenge but, fortunately, hasn’t dropped the ball.

It's out on Switch 2, too - and the upgrade is free.

Card Shark is the kind of game that at first blush seems like it just won’t work. Lots of dialogue bookended by brief, simplistic minigame sequences seems like it would make for an experience that would lose its lustre quickly, yet we couldn’t put it down.

Witty writing, high-stakes gameplay, and a gorgeous art style all come together here to make for a game that’s well-executed and unique in its appeal. If you’re looking to try something awesome that notably bucks most modern gaming trends, Card Shark is absolutely something we’d recommend, well worth your time and money.

Catherine: Full Body is a fantastic revamp of a bona fide cult classic. With an excellent new character and several new endings slickly inserted into an already highly entertaining narrative – not to mention a slew of fun new modes – this is the definitive version of an outstanding game.

If you've never played Catherine before, then you're in for an absolute treat, and if you have, we'd say there's enough new content here to make it worth diving in all over again.

An extremely impressive first game from The Wild Gentlemen, Chicken Police - Paint it RED! is one of the best visual novel/adventure games we've played in a long, long time and one hell of an absorbing tale. It looks and runs great on the Switch, with only a couple of really minuscule interface issues which are easily ignored.

At roughly eight or nine hours, the story is surprisingly lengthy, but we were never bored and wanted to investigate every little thing just to wring out more precious droplets of banter and fascination. Chicken Police is a polished, captivating experience and we're very excited for whatever's coming next from this team.

It's difficult to get across exactly why Danganronpa V3: Killing Harmony is so good without spoiling vast swathes of it, so we'll keep it simple. You'll come into the game baffled as to what the writers were thinking with some of these characters, and walk away loving each and every one of them.

There isn't a single moment of slack throughout the whole 40-hour playtime, it has the most extensive post-game of any title in the series, and one of the best endings to any game ever made. Go in blind and we promise you'll be in for the ride of your life.

Dark Souls: Remastered is a faithful remaster of a touchstone in video game design that improves overall performance of the original release while preserving all of the character traits that made it such a memorable experience. While it’s no less forgiving — and its menus are a little fiddly — this slick Nintendo Switch iteration offers an excellent way to experience Lordran’s ultra-challenging odyssey in true handheld form.

Plus, there's a Solaire of Astora amiibo. Praise the Sun, indeed.

This is an excellent port of a game that feels like it’s found a natural home on Switch thanks to a plethora of control options and the console’s natural facility with vertical orientation. Short of popping your 4K TV on its side, Switch offers the very best way to play Downwell.

Its roguelike structure and twitch platforming might not be for everyone, but you should really give it a chance. For our money, Downwell is a modern classic that should be in everyone’s collection; for the pocket change asking price, it's a steal.

Along with the expected multiplayer modes (ranked and casual battles), Faeria delivers a compulsive, interesting and frankly enormously fun card battle experience. While not the easiest game to explain, it's an impressive teaching tool for itself, but never feels overwrought or tiresome in said education. Of the card games we've enjoyed on Switch, Faeria is easily the highlight of the bunch and deserves to do well. It's a full-featured package and stands out as an excellent card/board/strategy experience. If you want to play a fantasy card game on Switch, we'd recommend this one first.

Every now and then, a game comes along that captures our hearts and reminds us why we love the medium in the first place. Forager features wonderfully designed crafting mechanics, addictive progression systems and more charm than you can possibly handle. Although it has very minor drawbacks, there's enough good stuff present here for us to confidently recommend adding Forager to your collection.

Heretic + Hexen is yet another slam dunk for Nightdive Studios. This new release revamps both titles with modern controls, bonus content, and thoughtful changes to the core design that make each game a delight to play.

Granted, these are still FPS titles from the mid-'90s, so your mileage will definitely vary, but for returning fans and those with a particular fondness for old-school 'boomer shooters', you really can't go wrong. Now let's get a native Switch 2 port with 120fps please, Nightdive.

Invisible, Inc. is a brilliant little tactics game, right up there with Into the Breach and XCOM – if not even better. The bite-sized structure belies a deceptively complex and meaningful game, where all your decisions ultimately mean something significant for that final desperate attack.

If you enjoy stealth or tactics games – or you're simply looking for a way into either genre – then Invisible, Inc. deserves your attention.

In a cynical era where nostalgia is pumped for all its worth with endless soulless remasters, Katamari Damacy Reroll serves up an engaging and rewarding game that hasn’t let any of its original charm or personality be lost in the transition from one platform to another.

With support for gyro controls and multiplayer — not to mention a degree of performance that sees it run smoothly in both handheld and docked mode — this Switch edition is easily the best way to play it outside of blowing the dust off your old PS2.

Altogether now: Naa na-na na-naa na na na...

An absolute pleasure from start to finish, what Kaze and the Wild Masks lacks in originality it makes up for in the strength of its level design, responsive controls, kinetic move set and attractive visuals. Excellent, action-packed platforming through and through, with great gameplay variety and gimmicks that don’t compromise on what the game is best at — challenging, fast-paced obstacle courses and deviously hidden secret areas.

Easiest sell? Kaze and the Wild Masks is to Donkey Kong Country what Freedom Planet was to Sonic the Hedgehog. Don’t miss this one.

Kirby and the Forgotten Land is a great big colourful joyride of an adventure for our little pink pal.

This first fully three-dimensional mainline entry in the franchise is bursting at the seams with fun and inventiveness, managing to transpose everything we know and love about past Kirby games to this all-new arena whilst adding plenty of delightful new aspects as it goes.

Mouthful Mode is daftly entertaining, each and every level is packed full of secrets and dripping in wonderful detail, and there are enough side activities, collectibles, and co-op fun here to keep you entertained and coming back for more for a good long while.

Whether you're playing on Switch 1 or via the excellent Star-Crossed World expansion on Switch 2 (with upgraded visuals and 60fps performance to boot), this comes highly recommended if you're looking for a fun platformer to play with kids.

Kirby and the Forgotten Land - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Star-Crossed World (say that five times, etc.) gives you the base game at a delicious 60fps with a whole big bunch of new content thrown in for good measure.

If you've had your fill of Forgotten Land on Switch 1, there's nothing here to warrant replaying the entire game again, but the 12 remixed areas that make up the DLC are uniformly delightful, the new transformations are excellent, and there's even new challenges for hardcore Kirby fans to get stuck into.

One of the best games on Switch and one of our favourite 3D platformers in years, polished to a sparkly sheen and packing some meaningful new content? That's a very easy recommendation and a truly excellent addition to the Switch 2's early lineup.

Buy Kirby and the Forgotten Land - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Star-Crossed World

Mark of the Ninja: Remastered is an utterly stellar stealth game and it’s lost none of the magic that made the original such a critical darling. Strong art direction, an engaging story, well-paced open gameplay, and a slew of extra content all combine to make for a near-flawless experience that you certainly won’t want to miss out on.

We’d give this game a high recommendation to all Switch owners; it’s the best stealth game money can buy in the Switch library, and one of the best ones in any console library.

Metroid Dread was a triumphant return for both Samus Aran and developer MercurySteam. This is a hugely entertaining and exquisitely designed entry that was slicker than anything we've seen from the series so far.

With a bunch of fantastic new abilities, super tense and enjoyable stealth sections, plenty of great big boss fights, and a story that long-time fans will definitely enjoy, we can't really see how this one could have been improved. Pixel nostalgia and genre impact aside, there's a very strong argument that 2D Metroid has never been better.

Monster Boy and the Cursed Kingdom is a tremendous accomplishment. It’s a gorgeous-looking game with a fantastic soundtrack and does its spiritual predecessors proud by nailing the Wonder Boy mechanics while still offering something that will appeal to modern audiences. As long as you can appreciate that it’s still very much an old-school game at heart and you’re going to get some 8-bit era platforming trickiness as a result, you’re going to thoroughly enjoy playing through this adventure for the 12-15 hours it’ll take you to beat it. It may not be Wonder Boy by name, but it’s definitely wonderful by nature.

Jim came to Nintendo Life in 2022 and, despite his insistence that The Minish Cap is the best Zelda game and his unwavering love for the Star Wars prequels (yes, really), he has continued to write news and features on the site ever since.

Not a bad price for Kirby and the Forgotten Land + Star Crossed World. If you haven't played it yet, this is a very good opportunity to grab a phenomenal game.

How does Slay the Spire only have a user score of 7.5?! What's wrong with you people?! I thought you were cool.

PSA regarding Faeria. I agree that it is outstanding game, and I’ve greatly enjoyed it - even as a solo player. But, last I checked, it still has an always-online requirement. Rather unusual for its genre.

Not a dealbreaker for me personally, but (understandably) a red line for others. Caveat emptor.

I picked up The Talos Principle and The Gardens Between on the cheap this week. The former will scratch my Portal-like itch for the time being.

#4161. Nioh 3 Comes To Xbox In January, Second Story DLC Launches Next Month

The Nioh series celebrates its 10th anniversary next February, and developer Team Ninja is celebrating with a pair of announcements for its latest entry, Nioh 3. First, the game's second story expansion, Bloody Insurrection, launches next month. Second, the game is coming to Xbox in January, marking the franchise's debut on Microsoft's platform.

Bloody Insurrection is Nioh 3's next story expansion following Hell Rising, which launched in August, and is set to release on December 18. Set in Shimabara in 1638, players will be at the center of a conflict between rebel forces, alchemists, and yokai while encountering familiar faces from previous Nioh games. Returning characters include Tachibana Muneshige from the original Nioh, and Bloody Insurrection will serve as the conclusion of protagonist Takechiyo's story.

Bloody Insurrection also introduces new Martial Arts for each weapon type, new Transformed Arts, Ninjutsu, Onmyo Magic, and Summoning Seals, and a new difficulty mode called Nioh's Journey. This new difficulty option is only available if you've completed the Enlightened One's Journey third playthrough and will allow players to find Ethereal equipment drops that let them acquire the highest rarity items in the game.

Additionally, Bloody Insurrection adds new endgame content called the Battlefield of Carnage. This challenges players with climbing floors, i.e., battlefields, filled with enemies and a boss. Each floor is divided into multiple battlefields, and defeating the floor's boss grants helpful battlefield effects, which can be combined to create unique synergies as you climb higher. Defeating enemies also lets players enhance special equipment "instilled with traces of the Yokai Realm," according to Koei Tecmo, which can only be found in Battlefield of Carnage.

A new edition of the game called Nioh 3: Complete Edition arrives on January 28 and will include the base game and its two story expansions. Complete Edition will arrive on PlayStation 5, PC, and, for the first time, Xbox Series X/S. The base version of Nioh 3 is also coming to Xbox Series X/S on the same date. The original version of Nioh 3 is also on sale at a 50 percent discount on PlayStation and Steam, and the season pass is 25 percent off.

For more on Nioh 3, be sure to read our review, in which we awarded the game a 9 out of 10. You can also check out our interview with Team Ninja discussing the Hell Rising expansion.

#4160. No more teasing, Arknights: Endfield finally has a January release date

Arknights: Endfield has been one of the most anticipated free-to-play 3D strategy games on the horizon, and it will be in our hands in the not-too-distant-future.

The Game Awards 2025 ceremony brought us yet more gacha game news, this time a big announcement for Arknights: Endfield. The free-to-play game set in the the universe of Arknights has been in various forms of closed tests for a while, but it finally has a release date.

The game is set to arrive simultaneously across PC, PS5, and mobile (iOS, Android) on January 22, and pre-registrations continue to be open.

Gryphline broke the news on The Game Awards stage alongside a chunky trailer featuring a new OneRepublic song. It actually ends up being a nice tone piece for the world of Arknights, showing a lot of cinematics alongside the music itself.

The developer-publisher also announced that so far, Arknights: Endfield has had over 30 million pre-registrations worldwide since pre-registrations went live. Some players have been able to play early, of course, with the most recent opportunity being Beta Test 2.

If you’ve been following the game’s development, you’ll know that it was pretty clear we’re closer than ever to the official launch. The most recent beta build showed off polished content, with new animations and cutscenes.

We’ve been playing it ourselves, and we think you’re going to agree with our Arknights: Endfield character tier list. You can expect more coverage from us as we get closer to launch, and when the game actually arrives.

Though it might seem like it came out of nowhere, the game is based on the Arknights universe, itself a massive mobile game with over 100 million downloads. Endfield brings a different flavour to that world, with a mix of strategy, exploration and real-time combat, not unlike the many games created by HoYoverse.

You can pre-register yourself on the official website.

#4159. Diablo 4's next expansion is bringing two new classes to the game, one of which you can play right now

Lord of Hatred may finally make good on the Mephisto arc of Diablo 4's campaign, which started in the original game and carried through Vessel of Hatred.

Very much when we expected it, Blizzard has officially revealed Diablo 4’s next major expansion at The Game Awards. Lord of Hatred delivers a new campaign that continues the mainline story, picking up from where Vessel of Hatred left off. Mephisto, the eponymous Lord of Hatred, has seemingly finally escaped imprisonment to rule over Sanctuary.

Lord of Hatred is the second Diablo 4 expansion, and it will be available on PC, PS5, Xbox One, and Xbox Series X/S on April 28.

It’s always a big deal when we get a new Diablo expansion, especially for a game as starved of fresh (major) content as Diablo 4 has been. But perhaps the biggest piece of news out of the Lord of Hatred reveal is that the expansion is bringing not one, but two new classes to the game.

The first of which is The Paladin, whereas the second is being kept under wraps. Even more surprising is that The Paladin is playable right now for anyone who pre-purchases the expansion. This is a well-timed shadow drop, especially given that Diablo 4’s latest season has just kicked off.

The expansion adds a new region to the world: Skovos, which is where the events of the new campaign will be taking place. This is the first time Skovos has been in a Diablo game. The region is of major significance to the world and lore of the series, as it is the birthplace of the firstborn, home of Lilith and Inaruis.

Lord of Hatred brings a decent number of major systems to Diablo 4. The endgame is getting a big overhaul, headlined by the new War Plans feature. Through this, you can effectively design your own endgame grind, creating challenges based on the activities you like and earning rewards along the way.

Endgame activities now also feature their own skill trees, which can be progressed through by creating War Plans for your character featuring each activity. The new endgame activity, Echoing Hatred, is something of horde mode where you must defend against unrelenting waves of enemies.

None of that matters without loot, of course, and the upcoming expansion is bringing back the Horadric Cube, and adding set bonuses using the Talisman system. The long-awaited and highly-requested Loot Filter is also coming to the game with the release of the expansion.

Beyond itemisation, each class’ skill tree will grow with new bonus skill variants. In fact, the entire skill system is being reworked for all classes - though details are a little sparse at the moment.

You can also expect the level cap to go up, which is very likely necessary to fit all the new skills and various systems. Blizzard offered a deep dive into the new Paladin class, which you see on the official blog.

#4158. The highly-anticipated follow-up to Baldur's Gate 3 is more Divinity, but it's not technically Original Sin 3

Larian has returned to tease a grand vision for its next major project, a new Divinity.

Larian Studios has delivered what was arguably the biggest reveal of The Game Awards 2025 showcase. The Hellstone, the mysterious monolith in the desert that’s been generating a lot of speculation in the lead-up to the show was indeed teasing the studio’s next game.

The Belgian developer is returning to the series it created with Divinity, a non-numbered sequel that’s designed for new and veteran players alike. The announcement was entirely cinematic, setting the tone for what looks to be the next big thing in the space.

Larian calls Divinity its most ambitious title ever, with the studio striving for a level of depth and breadth we’ve not seen before. This is the next project from the Baldur’s Gate 3 team, after all, so there’s understandably immense anticipation for it.

Divinity is a standalone RPG, and does not require you to have played Divinity: Original Sin, or Divinity: Original Sin 2. If you did, however, you’re going to find the journey extra special because of the continuity it offers.

“We’re ready to bring everything we’ve done previously into one place,” said founder and game director, Swen Vincke.

“This marks the beginning of something with more breadth, depth, and intimacy than anything we’ve created before. We’ve been building toward this moment ever since we took our fate into our own hands. This is the Divinity we’ve always wanted to make and you're going to have loads of fun with it.”

Beyond that, there’s precious little that’s been revealed for Divinity so far. We don’t know what platforms it’s going to be coming to, nor do we even have a release target. We do know it’s an RPG, so you can very much expect something similar to earlier games in the series, and, of course, Baldur’s Gate 3.

#4156. Arc Raiders' Cold Snap update brings snow storms to most maps, new events and a new Raider Deck

Arc Raiders has delivered a big new update that's very fittingly on theme, and it's not without new mechanics.

Arc Raiders is kicking off its last major event of the year. The Cold Snap update arrives moments from now, and it’s perhaps the game’s biggest since its momentous launch in late October. We’ve known about the existence of Cold Snap for a while, of course, but we finally have a solid idea about what to expect.

Cold Snap is made up of different components - including new content - that all players have access to.

As the name suggests, of course, Cold Snap introduces the new snowfall Map Condition. As part of this, maps will be covered in snow, thanks to snowstorms sweeping across them. For one, snowfall makes it harder to see enemies, but it also turns all lakes solid.

There’s a new mechanic associated with this, and it’s actually similar to Battlefield 6’s Winter Offensive update. Staying outdoors for too long will cause you to catch frostbite, which slowly drains HP. Embark says you’re going to need to bring more healing items with you on raids, and it doesn’t look like there are firepits that could keep you warm - though staying indoors for a while will help.

Cold Snap arrives alongside limited-time events that will be available until Tuesday, January 13. The snowfall visual update and new frostbite mechanics are available on Dam Battlegrounds, Buried City, Spaceport, and The Blue Gate.

One of the new events is Flickering Flames, which comes with its own progression track of 25 levels. Content is, of course, unlocked using Merits, which are earned from XP in matches. The other event is the Candleberry Banquet Project, which requires you to donate items found on the surface (including Candleberries).

You’ll earn rewards each time, and each stage completed will reveal a new scene on the banquet table. Likewise, there are cosmetic rewards as part of each stage, and you can use it as a source of Merits, too.

While on the subject, the new update also kicks off a new Raider Deck (battle pass). Available from December 26, The Goalie Raider Deck is pretty much what you’d expect. You’ll find several pages of cosmetic and useful items. The new Deck will be available to all players for free.

#4155. GTA 6: How to Fast Travel

Adam Beck is a Canadian who has covered the gaming industry for over twenty years. He has a passion for RPGs, action, stealth and horror games.

When it comes to open world games, there’s nothing quite as dense as Grand Theft Auto 6. Rockstar has created one of the most impressive open world games ever, with so much to see and do. It becomes incredibly immersive, to the point where sometimes you want a little more game in the game. One specific feature that is a bit unconventional is the fast travel system, but just how do you do it?

Find Selkie Hole in GTA 6, grab scuba gear, and explore the underwater cave system for meteorites and the Explorer’s Knife.

The obvious question a lot of people might have is “is there fast travel in Grand Theft Auto 6?” This is a massive game with a lot of things to see and do. It’s one of the most densely packed games we’ve ever played, and being an open world, one would expect there to be some sort of fast travel system.

You’ll probably go through a good portion of the game not realizing this, but there is indeed a fast travel system. This is because, even though it’s introduced to you early in the game, it’s something easily overlooked. With that said, it does come with a bit of a caveat to the point, especially early on, it’s not really worth using.

With all of that said, the way you can fast travel is through your phone. First, you will need to put a destination on your map. It can be a custom pin, or it can be a specific location such as a mission marker or clothing store.

Once you have this selected, bring up your phone and select the RydeMe app. This will bring up a standard menu showing how much it will cost to travel that distance you inputed (you can change the destination in this menu) along with ordering a Premium Ryde.

Select the ride and a car will appear shortly. Getting in, though, won’t immediately teleport you to that location. Instead, there will be dialogue, especially if you’re with your partner, and sometimes it is worth it to listen.

With that said, if you want to actually teleport, you can pay the driver an extra $100 to skip the ride and get there immediately. The downside is obviously, early on, this is an expensive way of traveling. Also, it will pass time considerably because the car itself will take a long time to get to the destination without breaking any rules.

Whether or not you want to use the teleport system in GTA 6 will probably be determined how far a place is located, as anything under 4 or 5 miles generally isn’t worth paying for, but when it gets above that, it can be a bit of a stretch – unless you want to take a helicopter or plane.

Learn where to find Vice City International Airport in GTA 6, how to enter by air, road, or fence, and what happens when you steal a plane.

#4154. Hollow Knight: Silksong Free Sea Of Sorrow DLC Releases December 11

Team Cherry promised us an update on Hollow Knight: Silksong's Sea of Sorrow DLC today, and thankfully it was not a tepid one where the studio gave the expansion a loose release window way off in the future. It was a far firmer reveal confirming that the free addition to Silksong will be here far sooner than you might have expected.

The trailer for Sea of Sorrow was part of today's Cherry Time update, giving us a first look at what horrors Hornet will be up against next. That first look at the expansion was coupled with the reveal that it will be available on December 11, 2026, so in just 13 days. The DLC will be free to all Silksong owners, no matter which platform you play on.

There is a lot crammed into what is a relatively short trailer showcasing what Sea of Sorrow has to offer. We're shown Hornet battling new enemies, traversing new areas, and judging by the last thing we're shown right at the end of the trailer, she's learned how to fish. Hornet is shown standing on the shore, casting her thread into the water and immediately getting a bite.

Although Team Cherry promised Silksong would be getting an expansion, Hollow Knight fans were fearful because we've been there before. Silksong itself was originally supposed to be DLC for the original Hollow Knight. However, the project wound up becoming so big that Team Cherry eventually decided it should be its own sequel. I'm sure Hollow Knight fans wouldn't argue with that decision given the benefit of hindsight, but it made the wait for Silksong especially excruciating.

There is no risk that Sea of Sorrow will be held back and used to complete the Hollow Knight trilogy. The expansion's release isn't even getting pushed into 2027. This time in two weeks, we'll all be playing it, and it won't cost you an extra penny to do so. If you own Silksong, you will get the DLC for free on December 11. And if you don't, the base game is still just $19.99 and is about to get a whole lot bigger.

Giving fans roughly two weeks between announcement and release appears to be a cadence that Team Cherry has settled into. There was roughly a two-week gap between the announcement of Silksong's release date and its launch, and that went incredibly well. I can only imagine repeating that pattern for Sea of Sorrow will have a similar effect, and the sequel will get a huge player count spike on December 11, along with a sales spike between now and then as those who missed out at launch play catch up before Sea of Sorrow arrives.

Take Sherma's guiding song everywhere with you.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#4153. Talking Point: Ocarina Of Time Revolutionised The 3D Swordfight, But How Does The Remake Hold Up In A Vintage Year For Clashing Blades?

Forget the hubbub around Grand Theft Auto. Big Walk? Big deal. It’s all noise designed to distract us from 2026’s real legacy: that it’s been one of the best years on record for video game swordfighting.

Onimusha: Way of the Sword broke free of parryslop with exciting, flexible and immensely satisfying katana combat. Blood of Dawnwalker’s directional combat recreated a scintillating sense of strike-and-counterstrike rhythm rather than asking players to hide behind defensive blocks. Then Phantom Blade Zero swans in with cinematic style and a dazzling flurry of wuxia sword strikes and somersaults.

It makes it a funny time for The Hero of Time to step back into the fray. After all, the original N64 Ocarina of Time practically set the template for today’s sword-toting successors. Dark Souls, Onimusha, even Kingdom Hearts’ keyblade battles all follow in Link’s Kokiri bootprints.

Ocarina of Time famously defined the lock-on, circle strafing, and the basic choreography of action-game design. According to a 2011 Iwata Asks, that genre-defining 3D swordfighting had a charming origin story (after a fleeting moment where they considered making Ocarina of Time in first-person!). It came about thanks to a ninja show witnessed by co-director Toru Osawa and colleagues on a frankly enviable work excursion to the Toei Kyoto Studio Park.

As Osawa remembered the Japanese period film reenactment, “a number of ninja were surrounding the main samurai, and one lashed out with a kusarigama [a sickle and chain weapon]. The lead samurai caught it with his left arm, the chain stretched tight, and the ninja moved in a circle around him.”

Action choreography was the remaining issue for director Yoshiaki Koizumi. At that same ninja show, he spotted the action movie routine that helps Jackie Chan inexplicably survive every movie:

“First, one attacks while the others wait. When the first guy goes down, the next one steps in and so on [...] Watching that show at the studio park was a clue toward solving that problem. Z-targeting flags one particular opponent, telling the other enemies to wait.”

That impeccable logic meant Link was safe from being mobbed by Keese swooping from offscreen in all directions. It was such a sound design principle that it continues to underpin action games today. But I suspect modern players no longer need to be handled with Koizumi’s kid gloves. Judging by the remake, Nintendo agrees.

Consider how Nintendo changed N64 Ocarina’s Forest Temple’s ominous fight against two Wolfos. Lock on to one, its counterpart scampers obediently into the background. Not so for the remake! These newly terrifying fiends aren’t just tankier, swifter, and more aggressive: they’ll conduct somersaulting tag-team switchups at will so you’re left to deal with a full health bar – just like the Lizalfos duo.

It’s a lesson not every Ocarina successor learned. The latest Onimusha’s greatest flaw comes from how closely its mobs follow the age-old formula. Attacking one at a time, queuing up a procession of theatrical wind-up animations makes them trivially easy for a supremely talented Mushashi to attack, deflect, or even decapitate with a well-timed Issen counter. Dawnwalker’s usually not much better, sending vampire Brencis’s lackeys after you in patient succession.

In comparison, I have to commend Phantom Blade Zero for its willingness to toss out Koizumi’s Law, never passing up an opportunity to give players a well-deserved backstabbing.

But the remake’s multitude of combat changes go far beyond footwork and newly aggressive enemies. For all its modernising under-the-hood changes, playing it still feels like entering a mystical parallel universe where Sekiro never happened. I’m back with sword and shield in hand, without a high-risk, high-reward parry ability.

Even with its snappier, flashier but deeply familiar combat, it took some getting used to a gentler pace compared to more recent upstarts. I started my playthrough thoroughly parrybrained after spending nearly 100 hours playing Dawnwalker into Wolverine before finally catching up with Metroid Dread. When I returned to Hyrule, it was with fingers already twitching with anticipation at every incoming blow.

Shorn of a now-trendy stamina meter, the fact that locking on to an enemy automatically raises your shields reduces the jeopardy; when I get hit, it’s because I got greedy.

One problem: I was ready to parry but Link wasn’t. In fact, the remake felt close to playing Dark Souls using the almost obligatory sword-and-shield build (with a parry I never learned to use properly!). As our review rightly noted, it’s laudably true to the original game, not even touching The Wind Waker’s combat-geared flourishes like the jump-spin attacks that would follow five years later.

The result is combat that feels almost like a cautious game of chess. You bait a mistake or trigger a weakness before going for the stunlock. Shorn of a now-trendy stamina meter, the fact that locking on to an enemy automatically raises your shields reduces the jeopardy; when I get hit, it’s because I got greedy. It may no longer be dangerous to go alone, but at least we have a few tips to help up the ante – I just wouldn’t recommend a swordless run!

Along with the absent stamina and posture meters, Ocarina remake’s simpler combat blessedly ignores a more recent swordfighting innovation: light and heavy attacks. Generally, I can live without the added layer of combat timing fussiness the Soulslike dominion has given us. It also avoids the pitfalls introduced by Phantom Blade Zero, where single inputs translate into a continuous flurry of attacks that can feel unsatisfyingly disconnected from the buttons I’ve pressed.

That’s not to say I wouldn’t say no to all modern embellishments. I’d love a high-powered combo finisher such as Wind Waker’s. But don’t forget: Ocarina already had a more entertaining means to deal a slow wind-up finishing blow capable of leaving its victim in a 6ft deep crater. It’s big, it’s bad, it’s the same height as your dad: it’s the Biggoron Sword!

But no matter the size of the sword he wields, Link’s return from the past has the vibe of a strangely youthful veteran checking in on his proteges. Musashi, Coen, and Soul are the new kids on the block, but they learned everything they know from their green-tunicked, rosy-cheeked master.

And if it ever comes down to a showdown, those newcomers simply aren’t getting past Link’s guard when he hasn’t got a stamina meter to wear down.

#4152. Witchbrook Has Officially Gone Gold

The long-awaited cozy magical sim game Witchbrook has officially gone Gold, developer Chucklefish announced today. For those unfamiliar with the term “Gold," it generally means the game is complete and ready to be submitted to platforms for certification (and is less likely to be delayed).

Witchbrook is set to launch on January 28, ending a development cycle that stretches back nearly a decade. First teased in 2017, Witchbrook is a life-sim where players control a witch who begins life in the seaside town of Mossport. This includes making friends, finding love, and, most importantly, enrolling in Witchbrook College to master magic by taking classes and completing assignments.

We're delighted to announce that Witchbrook has GONE GOLD ALL PLATFORMS! 💛 We're can't for you all to join us on the journey on Jan 28th! ✨[image or embed]

Witchbrook is more or less Stardew Valley meets Hogwarts Legacy, as you can also start and run businesses, engage in seasonal events, and interact with fully fleshed-out citizens who have daily routines and schedules to consider. After a development cycle marked by long stretches of silence and several delays, those anticipating Witchbrook can breathe easier knowing the game will more than likely stick to its release date.

When Witchbrook launches on January 28, it will be available on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, Xbox One, Switch, and PC.

#4151. Arc Raiders' latest patch adds two of the most requested features, but kills Cred hoarding

The last major Arc Raiders update of the year has arrived, bringing several big new features to the game, but not without some bad news.

Embark has just rolled out patch 1.7.0 for Arc Raiders players everywhere. This is a significant patch for the extraction shooter for a number of reasons, not least of which because it kicks off a series of events under the Cold Snap banner, which introduces a new conditions to the game’s maps.

Dig deeper into the patch notes, however, and you’ll find even more to get excited about, including features players have been asking for since the game’s first public test.

To start with, today’s update finally adds an option toggle aiming down sights. This is especially relevant for PC players, most of whom play shooters with an ADS toggle, rather than hold. Another often requested feature has been the ability to reset the game’s skill tree.

This is now available for the cost of 2,000 Coins per skill point. It goes without saying that you’re going to need a whole lot of money to reset the entire thing, but it’s a useful option to have when you want to alter your path.

The next change is one that’s going to ruffle a lot of feathers. Arc Raiders now has a soft Cred cap of 800. This is now clearly shown on your Wallet screen, and the developer said the cap is necessary to prevent players from using their accumulated Cred to unlock new Raider Decks immediately after release.

The good news is that this won’t affect the Cred you may already have, but going forward, 800 is the most you can hold at any point. You’ll also notice that Shani has more stuff for you to buy with Cred, in case you want another way to spend what you have.

Patch 1.7.0 also brings a few other additions - and makes some changes - that are worth highlighting. You can now customise your Raider Tool, which likely means we’re going to see Raider Tool cosmetics going forward.

Speaking of items, the Aphelion weapon blueprint has been moved to Stella Montis, so you won’t be able to get it from taking down the Matriarch. The Bettina, and Rattler have both seen some balance changes.

The Bettina’s durability will now degrade a lot slower per shot, making it take 26 magazines to fully deplete durability. The base magazine size has been increased to 22, and the reload time has been cut to 4.5 seconds. Embark says this should make the weapon more viable in PvP, while also allowing it to stand on its own without the need for players bring a secondary weapon.

As for the Rattler, the only change it gets is an increase to its magazine size from 10 to 12. The idea is to make it about as effective as a Stitcher or Kettle at close ranges when it comes to PvP encounters.

And, of course, it wouldn’t be a big Arc Raiders patch without some tweaks to the game’s Arc enemies. This time, the Shredder gets all the love. The menacing unit now moves faster, turns more sharply and doesn’t get knocked back as much when shot.

The Shredder’s head now has more health, too, meaning you won’t be able to shoot it off early and confuse it. In general, the Arc unit should be smarter, especially when navigating narrow spaces. Finally, the Shredder now activates faster upon detecting (and being attacked by) players.

Beyond that, the main menu has seen a few changes to highlight ongoing events, make certain announcements quieter, make it easier to track Raider Quests and more. There’s a lot more in this update, too, such as changes to footstep loudness, several tweaks to loot and the value of certain items, and more besides. You’ll find the full change log on the official website.

#4150. It’s official: Battlefield 6 is 2025's best-selling game, but Black Ops 7 still managed to be November’s top-seller

2025 will be remembered for many things, but in the ultra-competitive games industry, it’s going to be thought of as the year Battlefield 6 did what many thought couldn’t happen.

Circan’s November 2025 video game sales report has easily been one of the most anticipated. For one, November is always one of the most lucrative for the games industry, but this year in particular has seen several major hits - including new entries in two rival series.

We’re talking, of course, about Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 the latest releases in their respective multiplayer shooter series. The decades-old fight to claim the top spot has long been won by Call of Duty, but the latest Battlefield has achieved what many thought was impossible.

Cricana’s report covers spending on video game software, hardware, and accessories in the U.S. November 2025 saw spending fall by 4% compared to November 2024, bringing in a total of $5.9 billion.

Software technically saw growth during the month, but declines in hardware, and accessories were mainly responsible for the drop in overall spending. Black Ops 7 continued Call of Duty’s 18-Year Streak in topping sales in its launch month.

However, this year’s game did not also top the year-to-date charts, something the series has done consistently, and more than any other top-selling game each year - with rare exceptions. Battlefield 6 is firmly in the lead there, cementing its claim as 2025’s best-selling title. Black Ops 7, fittingly, occupies in the #7 spot there.

Separately from the best-selling game title fight, November has actually been one of the worst for the industry in terms of hardware sales. The report notes that the three major platform holders - Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo have all seen their hardware sales decline.

Spending on hardware during November amounted to only $695 million, a massive 27% decline compared to November 2024. According to the report, that’s the worst dollar amount total for any November since 2005, when it comes to hardware specifically. All three current-gen consoles totaled 1.6 million units sold, which Circana also notes is the lowest for any November since 1995.

This all doesn’t bode especially well for the industry. November has always been a key holiday shopping month, but it’s clear the constantly rising console prices - and already high game prices - have had a big impact.

#4148. I Hate Video Game Romance – Here's Why Grand Theft Auto VI Is The Exception

Generally speaking, I do not like romance mechanics in video games. I never find them convincing. Relationships build way too quickly, and usually all it takes to win someone over in an RPG or farming sim is a couple of conversations and a few gifts. In Grand Theft Auto VI, however, I'm extremely invested in the romance between Jason and Lucia, and it comes down to the game's quieter moments and slice-of-life mechanics.

If you've played Baldur's Gate 3, Stardew Valley, Date Everything, or practically any other game with romance options, you're familiar with the gameplay loop. I ask an NPC about her hometown, sympathize with her tragic backstory, promise to be there for her, and then give her the book, cake, or mining resource she likes. Do it enough, and one day she'll approach me with the uncharacteristically heartfelt confession that she can't stop thinking about me. The process is too transparently mechanical: I can scan the dialogue options and instantly know which of the three sentences will boost my affinity rating the most. It feels less like an actual relationship and more like a long-term scheme to program someone into dating.

Many games structured like the ones above are written as well as they can be. The issue is scope and structure. Romantic relationships are nuanced and unique, but there often aren't enough resources during a game's development to represent more than the basic building blocks. Players are meant to suspend disbelief and fill in the gaps – even though you technically only spoke to that villager a few dozen times, you're married with a child, so you imagine it's actually been years.

Of course, this scope is the difference between Grand Theft Auto VI and these other games – Rockstar made time and space for everything in this world, and romance is no exception.

Since they're dating when the game begins, Jason and Lucia admittedly skip the courtship phase that many games focus on, but their relationship is still conditional and malleable – if you want them to like each other, you should be acting in their best interests. And while the mechanical aspect of their romance is still plenty visible, the actions to increase that meter are vastly expanded. There has been a lot of discussion about the early game, when you can prep for Lucia's release from prison by buying flowers or groceries, and while I like those gestures, they're not what sold me on the relationship. Say what you will about modern dating standards, but flowers and food are too easy – too obvious for me to feel connected to and invested in a couple.

When I played this section, I felt like Jason's hair looked a little unkempt, so I got a shave and a haircut. And, to my surprise, this improved his relationship with Lucia. She wasn't around and wouldn't see the results until later, but it still scored me partner points, as did repairing the roof, painting the bedroom walls, and even giving Jason's car a new paint job. These unexpected, specific tasks don't just fill up the relationship gauge – they communicate information about both characters. Lucia is really looking forward to getting out of prison, and having a finished house and a clean, put-together partner sets her in a better mood. Meanwhile, my actions establish that my version of Jason knows she likes these things and would do them without even asking.

Minor, specific tasks like these are romantic because they imply a degree of thoughtfulness that sidesteps the grand gestures expected of a long-awaited reunion. Yes, there should be apples in the fridge, but that's a basic need; knowing the exact conditions Lucia wants the house to be in makes me believe Jason actually knows her. It becomes even more effective – both in real relationships and in the credibility of the in-game partnership – when thoughtfulness is demonstrated on a day-to-day basis, in the quiet moments.

Grand Theft Auto VI is a long game with a slow, steady pace, leaving room for the intimate interactions other games wouldn't have time for. If you come home at the end of the day and see your partner watching TV, you can sit next to them and get a bonus. When they go to sleep, they'll call out to you and ask you to lie in bed and scroll on your phone with them. You can hold hands in public, buy each other clothes, and remember to text back promptly. There are large, dramatic moments and professions of love, yes, but players are likely to experience vastly more of these minor interactions than those scripted cutscenes.

Romance can be flashy, but it has to be more than that. It's nice to see the starring duo dance, drive, and shoot at foes during cutscenes. But it's the long car rides when Lucia reassures Jason that her mom likes him, or the evening on the couch when Jason talks about how he likes the way Lucia laughs, that make this relationship work narratively.

#4146. GTA 6: How to Get into the Apocalypse Bunker

Adam Beck is a Canadian who has covered the gaming industry for over twenty years. He has a passion for RPGs, action, stealth and horror games.

What’s Grand Theft Auto 6 without a conspiracy theorist character? That’s exactly who Freddie is, a man with his own podcast, and he’s ready for the apocalypse in his big bunker. Unfortunately, you won’t know where to find Freddie as his location is somewhat obscure. There’s nothing to point you in the right direction, but thankfully, that’s why we’re here. We know exactly where to find this bunker, but be warned: it’s not as easy to breach as most hideouts.

Find out how to get into bank vaults in GTA 6, complete Yasmani’s Lombank robbery, escape the police, and get tips on more vaults.

The bunker in Grand Theft Auto 6 is a little trickier to find just because it doesn’t quite point you in the right direction. This isn’t part of a main quest, let alone a side quest, but instead is something that has to be found by exploring.

The bunker in question is located in North Leonard County. This section of the map can be found east of North Kelly County and northwest of Vice City itself. The biggest landmark you can look for on the map is Lake Leonida. The bunker can be found on the northwest road closest to it. You see several dark-colored buildings on the map.

Upon driving up to it, though, you will notice that it is completely fortified with an intercom and an automated message saying automated defenses will end you if you attempt to get in.

Being locked away, there will be the temptation to get in. Thankfully, the first time you do this, it’s relatively easy. If you head to the northeast corner of the bunker’s fence, you will find a water tower with a multi-ladder climb.

Climb up the first ladder and on the small platform, jump over the fence onto the shack below. Congratulations; you have successfully breached the defenses. Unfortunately, it’s not over quite yet. This is because there will be additional defenses set up.

Specifically, there will be landmines spread across the property. The best you can do is go down the road towards the bunker and keep an eye out on the ground. You will hear beeping and a red dot on the mine when you get too close.

When you get close to the bunker, drones will be activated. Simply shoot the two down before they get too close as they will explode and deal a good deal of damage. Afterward, jump down the small slope and walk up to the bunker.

The resident, Freddie, isn’t happy you have got as far as you have, but sees it as a challenge to up his defenses. He will say he will text you when he has installed a better system. Simply wait until he texts you before heading back.

The second time is a little trickier to get in only because he has blocked ladder access to the water tower. Thankfully, he left some excavating tools out in the northwest of the perimeter.

There will be a truck with a large bed, and a bulldozer. Park the truck close to the electric fence and then use the bulldozer’s blade to lift the bed of the truck until it’s slightly above the fence. Jump on the truck and into the bed and then hop over the fence. It’s best to set this up near the water tower to avoid some mines.

Speaking of which, the mines are now a little harder to detect. This is because they’re buried slightly further underground, and you can’t see the red light when you get near them. You will still be able to hear it, but it’s best to use your Focus Mode to see them as they light up.

Moving down the road, avoiding the significantly more placed mines, the drones attack has also been adjusted. He will still send two waves of them, but instead of one at a time, the first wave has two drones and the second has three.

After taking care of them, jump down the slope again and approach the bunker for you to meet Freddie for the first time. Congratulations! You can now enter the bunker and even hang out with the apocalypse-ready Freddie.

#4145. GTA 6 Easter Egg Hints Jason And Mandy Have History

Day one, a lot of players were thirsting over Mandy in GTA 6. Jason visits her house shortly before Lucia is let out of prison to fix her sink, and the sleaziest VHS tape tucked away in the attic slowly starts to unfold, as she strips down to a bikini and poses right in front of your handyman. Obviously, nothing happens, but it's not over just because Jason slinks away, even if Mandy's role in the story at this point is practically non-existent.

There's the whole serial killer conspiracy, as players spotted her cleaning blood in her bathroom, sparking some wild theories — like Mandy being responsible for Leonida's string of missing persons. If you try to follow her into the bathroom, she even texts you saying that "if you weren't so hot I'd chop all your fingers off." But what's lesser known is that if you make a trip to a meditation spot as Lucia, there's an interesting flashback that seems to hint that Jason and Mandy have a history.

As reported by IGN, during one of these sequences, you can hear Jason saying, "Yeah, okay, we hooked up once, but, you know, barely. And it was a long time ago. You don't need to worry about her, Lu. Have you seen you? I know how good I got it. I'm not gonna screw that up again."

Jason doesn't mention her by name, but this dialogue seems to come after Lucia was sprung from jail, right around the time the two would've been chilling in the keys by Mandy's house. It'd be a little odd for a flashback to reference an unknown woman the player has no connection to, and knows nothing about. Still, it could be a total stranger, so it's worth taking with a grain of salt, but it would certainly explain Mandy's... obsession.

A Floridian real estate listing has gone viral, but it isn't actually the house that inspired Jason's home in GTA 6.

As Twitter user Lanzino pointed out, towards the end of Act 1, you can sneak up on Mandy while she's talking to a police officer, and she has a few lines that stand out. "I wanted to light his house on fire so many times," she cries. "But I couldn't. I loved him too much! I always thought I had time, you know, to change his mind."

Get close enough and Lucia even calls her a "cray b****." GTA 6 is full of these tiny little mysteries weaved throughout the open world and narrative, and Mandy is a hot-spot for them. If her and Jason really did have history together, and she really is the Leonida Butcher, then maybe it's for the best he broke it off.

The most anticipated video game of all time is a triumph on every level that exceeds years of unbelievable expectations. You're not ready for Leonida.

#4144. GTA 6's Physical Launch Has Been An Astronomical Success, Despite No Discs

All eyes have been on the launch of GTA 6 this month, with the game's so-called physical launch being a particularly interesting litmus test for the future of the industry.

It turns out that even without any discs, GTA 6 has proven to be a monumental success in terms of physical sales. This comes via Christopher Dring at The Game Business, who states that the game enjoyed the largest physical launch since 2019 in the UK, generating £32 million in revenue in just three days.

He goes on to state that GTA 6 is the "No.17 biggest physical game launch in the UK since records began in 1995".

In France, it's estimated that over 1 million physical copies were sold in the first three days, a figure that Dring states is comparable to GTA 5 back in 2013. In Spain, meanwhile, the game achieved the largest physical launch in the chart's history.

It's safe to say then that this has comfortably dwarfed pretty much anything that Nintendo has put out in recent years. Normally of course, we'd be celebrating such success – even if the game isn't actually available on Nintendo systems – but the fact that it's a code-in-a-box release raises a few eyebrows.

With GTA 6 being such a success, Sony will no doubt view this as validation that it made the right decision in ceasing the production of discs from 2028. Other large companies will also likely see it as proof that customers don't care about discs anymore, and will likely lean toward download codes much sooner than Sony's cut-off date.

Nintendo itself, meanwhile, probably won't do anything different – at least for the time being. Stats from recent financial reports indicate that Switch and Switch 2 players still value cartridges, with physical sales still making up close to half of the company's total first-party sales.

Still, it's a troubling result for folks who are still all-in on physical games. It certainly indicates that while there are plenty of folks who begrudge Sony's decision to stop the production of discs, there are many, many more people who just don't give a hoot.

#4143. Rockstar Reportedly Shopping Around Red Dead Redemption TV/Movie Rights, But Has Rejected Grand Theft Auto Adaptation Offers

Grand Theft Auto VI hasn't even been out for a week, and yet it's shattering records left and right, following in the footsteps of its predecessor, Grand Theft Auto V. Despite that, developer Rockstar Games has reportedly continued to reject Hollywood TV and film adaptation offers for the crime saga series, according to a report from The Ankler. However, the studio is reportedly more open to a TV or film adaptation of its cowboy western series, Red Dead Redemption, according to the same report.

The Ankler reports that Rockstar is looking at possible licensing deals for its long-running western shooter series, which received its last entry in 2018, Red Dead Redemption II, for as much as $100 million. There's heavy emphasis on "possible," though, as there is no confirmation that Rockstar has said yes to any of these offers thus far. It's very likely a TV or film adaptation might never come to fruition – it's common for studios to field offers like this, sometimes with serious intent and other times as a quick look at the ocean of possibilities, as it were.

That said, video game adaptations continue to grow more and more popular, especially compared to their humble beginnings in Super Mario Bros. (1993), DOOM, and Mortal Kombat. Franchises like Sega's Sonic the Hedgehog, CD Projekt Red's Cyberpunk 2077, renewed Super Mario Bros. and Mortal Kombat efforts, and others, including Street Fighter, Resident Evil, Fallout, and Castlevania, have found great success on streaming services and on silver screens. Given how beloved the narratives of Rockstar's Red Dead Redemption series are, it's not surprising that production studios are interested in adapting those stories for TV and movie theater screens.

In the meantime, players have plenty to experience from Rockstar via its latest release, Grand Theft Auto VI, which launched on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S last week on November 19. Speaking of that game, read Game Informer's Grand Theft Auto VI review to see why it's one of the greatest games we've ever played, and check out the patch notes for the game's first update.

#4142. Heartopia finally gets a release date... on everything but Steam

Heartopia may very well be the first big game you play in 2026.

Heartopia developer XD Games has delivered the news anyone who tried out the life sim game had been waiting for. The Animal Crossing-like cozy multiplayer game will finally arrive on January 7 across Android, iOS, and PC - with one caveat.

The Steam version won’t actually launch on that date, and will instead go live at some other point in the future. You will be able to play it on PC through TapTap, which is the same emulator you may be familiar with from beta.

Pre-registration is open on the official website for all platforms. If you throw in your email address, you’ll receive a bundle of in-game items at launch. You’ll get 4,000 Gold, 20 Wishing Stars, 400 Moonlight Crystal, and 60 Exhibition Passes.

Interestingly, XD Games isn’t saying what you can expect from the launch build - in terms of content - just yet. Those details will be revealed closer to the January launch, so perhaps expect them in the first few days of the year.

If you created a character in either (or both) of the recent closed beta tests, you’ll also receive the Blueberry Crossbody Bag in-game cosmetic. If you made it to level 18 in either test, you’ll also get the Star Mascot Head cosmetic. Both items will be available to claim at launch.

We’ve spent a lot of time playing the game’s recent tests, and we’ve put together some early guides on how to get Roaming Oak Timber, how to unlock and upgrade hobbies and more. We also have a few cooking recipes to share with you.

#4141. Legendary game creator Vince Zampella has passed away

Vince Zampella, co-creator of Call of Duty, and a veteran studio head responsible for some of the biggest franchises in the world, is gone.

Vince Zampella, known for co-creating the Call of Duty series, among many other roles, has died. Zampella, 55, died in a car crash in Los Angeles on Sunday. The fatal crash killed him, along with the occupant of his car.

According to NBC, Zampella’s Ferrari hit a concrete barrier after leaving a tunnel in the San Gabriel Mountains, north of Los Angeles. Zampella was unfortunately trapped in an ensuing car fire, and the passenger was ejected.

Vince Zampella is one of the industry’s most prolific creators. His storied career is long, and is responsible for some of the biggest shooter franchises in history. It started with Medal of Honor in the 90s, a game that changed WW2 shooters forever.

Zampella later co-founded the legendary Infinity Ward in 2002, the team that would go on to redefine multiplayer shooters forever. Infinity Ward is the studio responsible for the Call of Duty series, which remains one of the biggest games for publisher Activision, and the entire industry.

Zampella then left the studio he founded in 2010 following a major fallout with Activision. He, along with longtime collaborator, Jason West, went to rival publisher EA to form Respawn Entertainment.

Respawn went on to create the Titanfall series, and later Apex Legends. The studio is responsible for non-shooters, of course, like the third-person action game series Star Wars Jedi. Zampella was instrumental in making the game possible, having hired God of War 3 director Stig Asmussen to helm a team within Respawn out of a desire to diversify the studio’s output and prove he can do more than make shooters.

Zampella had only recently met with journalists and peers at The Game Awards, where Battlefield 6 was nominated for multiple awards. Battlefield 6 is the most successful game in series history, in part as a result of Zampella’s leadership. The legendary leader was given the reigns of the struggling multiplayer shooter franchise in 2021, with a goal of finding a viable future.

Zampella’s sudden death has shaken the industry, and many mourn his loss as the news started spreading.

“We are heartbroken by the loss of Vince Zampella, a creative leader whose work shaped generations of players and helped define what modern shooters and action games could be,” EA said in a statement.

“While his impact reached far beyond any one game or studio, we will remember Vince for how he showed up every day, trusting his teams, encouraging bold ideas, and believing in Battlefield and the people building it. We are deeply grateful for his leadership, his generosity, and the care he brought to everything he touched, and we will carry that forward with us.”

#4139. Love and Deepspace 5.0 update brings together all five love interests for the first time

Love and Deepspace is getting a big update to celebrate its second anniversary, and there's a lot to dig through.

If you can believe it, Love and Deepspace is almost two-years-old, and Infold Games is celebrating the moment in a few major ways. The Throne of Eros update brings the game up to version 5.0, and it’s one for fans of all love interests.

For one, this is the first time all five of them are brought together. The update is also adding some important new features, alongside anniversary events, and more.

Throne of Eros also doubles as the new Wish Pool, which is the one that has all of the game’s love interests in a single banner. This is a limited-time affair, of course, but it’s not the only thing you should look forward to here.

There’s also the Memory Growth Bonus, another limited-time event that you can take advantage of to grow your Memories. The even bigger news is that you can target your Wishes through the Xspace Echo, which lets you select five Memories to create your own pool from. You can use this to get any Memories you might not have, of course.

On the topic of Memories, you’ll also be able to unlock new second anniversary KV Memories, as part of a Yearly Highlights Event that will let you look back on your own journey with the game over the past year.

On the story and narrative side, Throne of Eros adds two new main stories, with new branches for Xavier, and Rafayel. There’s even a narrative-specific event that will run throughout the anniversary period, through which you can earn two daily outfits for each of the five love interests.

The celebrations also extend to new anniversary content like mail, and video calls. You can purchase a Yearly Pass, and check out some new arrivals at the Lunar Shop.

Beyond the anniversary content, version 5.0 also adds a new feature to the game: Home, which essentially offers a hub to get you directly to interacting with love interests that doesn’t have to do with combat or story.

You can also expect various other quality of life updates that touch on the Journal, Phone Moments Search, Resources Quick Cleanup, and new Tete-a-Tete that should make interacting with all of them more streamlined.

While this is a special banner, you should brush up on how banners work in Love and Deepspace if you’re unfamiliar. As always, it’s never not a good idea to check our Love and Deepspace codes page for some freebies.

#4138. GTA 6: Determining Raul’s Fate

Adam Beck is a Canadian who has covered the gaming industry for over twenty years. He has a passion for RPGs, action, stealth and horror games.

The open world Rockstar has created for Grand Theft Auto 6 is massive, but it’s not just about the weird random encounters you will find yourself in. There is a massive, 40+ hour-long story with a whole cast of characters to explore. One of the best characters introduced has to be Raul, a suave thief who Brian introduces to, and one who plays a key component to everything that happens in both chapter 3 and 4.

Unfortunately, like a number of minor characters in the story, there is a scene very late in chapter 4 where his fate seems to be put into your hands. We will go over both scenarios, although you might be a bit disappointed with the outcome.

Spoiler warning for anyone who hasn’t reached past the VCI Takedown mission.

Find Freddie’s apocalypse bunker in GTA 6 and learn how to get inside on both visits while avoiding landmines and drones.

The first option is pretty simple. Raul quickly tells you what happened, specifically, Valentina sold them out and Mendez personally came and tortured him. After that, he tells Lucia and Jason to put him out of his misery.

This is where the “choice” comes into play. This option will initiate a firefight outside the boat, as whoever finds Raul tied up will shoot him in the head. Thankfully, Raul comes ready for anything and has a gun locker in the other room.

Still, doing this yourself is arguably the best thing to do for Raul as he likely would have been killed more horrifically afterward. Still, if you don’t want to pull the trigger yourself, there is another option.

Despite Raul pleading and begging for Jason and Lucia to put an end to his suffering, there is the option to restrain yourself like you can in various other situations thus far. You don’t have to pull the trigger, but unfortunately, Raul’s fate is secured no matter what.

If you decide you can’t put Raul out of his misery yourself, your partner, specifically whoever doesn’t find Raul in the bathroom, will automatically shoot him instead. It’s a pretty anti-climatic conclusion, all things considered, especially considering the shot itself alerts a task force which is converging on the boat.

In the end, Raul must die for the story to continue, and either Jason or Lucia will be the one who pulls the trigger. It’s just a matter of if you, as the player, does it.

#4137. Genshin Impact Version Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, including the long-awaited Moon Maiden Columbina

The first major Genshin Impact update in 2026 is almost here, bringing characters we've been waiting a while to play, and more besides.

Genshin Impact’s latest Special Program has spilled all the beans on the game’s next major update, Luna 4. The update, which arrives on January 14, kicks off 2026 with several bits of new content, including some previously-teased characters.

Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.

The first new arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden. Columbina is a 5-Star Hydro Catalyst wielder. Her kit revolves around supporting the squad via Lunar Reactions. She can trigger coordinated Lunar Reaction DMG, even when she’s off the field.

The Moon Maiden’s special ability, Lunar Domain, further boosts all Lunar Reactions by applying a DMG bonus, including summoning more thundercloud strikes for Lunar-Charged reactions. Columbina is also capable of converting Electro-Charged, Bloom, and Hydro Crystallize reactions into Lunar Reactions, as well as revive fallen squad members.

Speaking of elemental reactions, new in this version is Lunar-Crystallize, a new reaction that’s triggered when Geo meets Hydro (under certain conditions). When triggered, Lunar-Crystallize summons three Moondrifts near enemies. When triggered three times, Moondrift Harmony gets activated, dealing Geo DMG to enemies caught in its radius.

Then there’s Zibai, an Adeptus from Liyue. Zibai is another 5-Star character, a Geo Sword wielder. Zibai can, through entering a special state where they can build up energy, unleash an Elemental Skill that deals Lunar-Crystallize DMG.

The longer the fight goes on, the more Lunar-Crystallize reactions are triggered, the higher (and more often) the damage of Zibai’s Elemental Skill becomes.

Luna 4 continues the Nod-Krai story arc, with a big confrontation with Il Dottore. This is the focus of the new Archon Quest, completing which will earn you a new outfit. There’s a gameplay element to that new chapter, too, with the reveal of Piramida, a new area north of the region. Piramida is the headquarters of the Lightkeepers.

The first phase of Luna 4’s Event Wishes will, unsurprisingly, feature Columbina. It’ll also include reruns of Ineffa. The second phase is when Zibai becomes available, alongside another newcomer: Illuga, a 4-Star, polearm-wielding Geo Lightkeeper. The second phase’s rerun will be Neuvillette, who’s also going to have a new outfit in the shop at a discount.

Version Luna 4 brings back the annual Lantern Rite event, taking place in the mainland of Liyue. The event features its own set of minigames with unique rewards, alongside new stories of the Adepti.

All around Liyue Harbor, you’ll be able to place Xiao Lanterns and inscribe them with messages for others to read. You’ll also earn some Fortune Coins from Auspicious Treasure Trees, which you can later exchange for gifts.

All players will receive 1,600 Primogems through the in-game mail. If you log in regularly, you can earn up to ten Intertwined Fates. Lantern Rite has a new outfit for Yaoyao, which is also where you have a chance to earn one 4-Star Liyue character for free.

Finally, you can look forward to the new Classic Mode in Miliastra Wonderland, which lets you invite select Teyvat characters to join you.

#4136. Fans Reject Universes Beyond In New MTG Set Poll From Mark Rosewater

It may be only a small sample of players, but the message is clear: Universes Beyond isn't going to win out over in-universe sets.

There have been a whopping seven Magic: The Gathering sets released this year, and players agree on one thing: it was way too many. Six is the standard figure expected moving forward, with a 50/50 split between in-universe and Universes Beyond.

Over on his Blogatog, Magic's lead designer, Mark Rosewater, held a poll asking players what their favorite set of 2026 was, and while the overall winner was a little predictable, there are still some surprising results, and none look particularly good for Universes Beyond.

In the poll held on his Blogatog, Mark Rosewater listed all seven sets, along with the option for "I refuse to pick one." The final results, which show that 2,695 people voted, indicate that Reality Fracture wins by a landslide at 44.8%, with the next closest set being Secrets of Strixhaven at 15.9%, followed by Lorwyn Eclipsed at 15.1%.

A bit of quick math shows that this already accounts for 75.8% of the total vote, and the next highest entry at 9% is the aforementioned pick refusal, which takes us to 84.8%. This leaves just over 15% spread across the remaining four sets, all of which were Universes Beyond offerings. Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles came in last with 2.2%, followed by The Hobbit at 2.5%, Star Trek at 4.3%, and finally Marvel Super Heroes at 6.3%.

This sample size isn't nearly big enough to represent anything beyond players tuned into Mark Rosewater's blog at the time of the poll, but it's still a scathing indictment of Universes Beyond, and it doesn't help the seemingly growing calls for change following Star Trek's failure.

The Universes Beyond sets are often extremely divisive, but some are much better than others, so we've ranked every one so far.

The biggest sign that Universes Beyond isn't going anywhere anytime soon is that Wizards of the Coast is already planning sets for 2030 and beyond, with the current yearly 50/50 split in mind. This would mean at least nine more Universes Beyond sets planned beyond 2027.

One thing we're starting to see with Universes Beyond is learning between sets. The original Universes Beyond sets that were Standard legal were in the works for so long that we're only now reaching a point where lessons learned from those sets are starting to impact the design of future ones.

Marvel Darkhold Destiny feels like the first set that's truly taking a lot of the fan feedback on board, which is leaning very heavily into adopting Marvel into the world of Magic using a brand new original story and character, rather than just smashing the two properties together and seeing what comes out the other side.

If we look at some of the biggest complaints about Star Trek, then we'd expect the main takeaways to be less reliance on properties that use real-life actors, far less artwork that is just 'character standing and pointing', and not taking mechanics and settings that could make for a great in-universe set (Star Trek could easily have been Edge of Eternities 2, for example) and wasting them on a Universes Beyond property.

Universes Beyond is a part of Magic now, and the best we can hope for is that it improves with each new release, and eventually even the loud minority who oppose it come round to enjoy (or tolerate) its inclusion.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#4135. Heartopia captures the hearts of Animal Crossing and The Sims fans to become the No.1 free download across 50 countries

Heartopia is officially the first big mobile launch of 2026, as the game grabs the attention of millions worldwide.

Heartopia, the new cosy life sim from XD Games, has officially arrived on mobile, right on schedule. If you’ve been keeping up with Heartopia news, you’re likely already aware that the game has pushed back its Steam release to an indeterminate point in 2026.

Doesn’t look like it mattered much, however, as this has already been a big launch on iOS and Android — it probably helps that PC players aren't being entirely left out of the fun, since the game is already available there via XD's own cross-device platform TapTap.

XD Games announced today that Heartopia has reached the top spot on the App Store’s downloads page for free games, and it managed to do so in more than 50 countries and regions worldwide.

The developer is celebratig by offering players a lot of free stuff. If you're feeling lucky, you’ll find new outfits and furniture in three gacha banners (Gilded Acorn Exhibitions): Polar Hymn, The Frostguard, and Coolplayism.

XD Games says you can expect regular updates to add more content, through Fashionwaves and Festivals. In fact, the first season - Winter Frost - is already penciled in for sometime in late January, and it’s going to add appropriately wintery activities like ice skating and snowman-building.

In February, a My Little Pony collaboration event will kick off, bringing new inspired outfits, and vehicles to the game.

Heartopia is a clever mix of Animal Crossing, and The Sims. It’s a free-to-play life sim where you can create your own character, dress them up, build a home for them (and decorate it), and go about town visiting and playing with other players’ characters.

The game’s main feature is the ability to take on a hobby, and seven of those are available at launch. You can dig deep into each hobby, either alone or with others, and there’s a progression track dedicated to each one.

Whether you’re among the millions who downloaded the game already, or you intend to so soon, we’ve got a set of helpful guides to get you started. You should check out how to unlock and upgrade hobbies in Heartopia first, before you get deep into finding all cooking recipes. And, of course, this wouldn’t be a big game launch without a bunch of Heartopia codes for some free stuff.

Rockstar's code-in-a-box release had a staggering debut week in Japan, pulling in over 200,000 physical sales and kicking Ocarina of Time's comparatively measly ~35,000 into second.
